ou.description:
Subproductos: 

7.2.1	Al 2022, las instituciones gubernamentales competentes, el sector privado, la academia y las comunidades cuentan con mecanismos de diálogo e instrumentos que permitan gestionar los recursos naturales, proteger y conservar la biodiversidad y los ecosistemas.

7.2.2	Al 2022, las instituciones gubernamentales locales, la academia, el sector privado y las comunidades cuentan con instrumentos que les permitan identificar y controlar las fuentes de contaminación para salvaguardar el medio ambiente, la salud humana y la de los seres vivos.

ou.parentName: ED7. Al 2025, el Edo. mexicano refuerza sus capacidades de adaptación y resiliencia frente a la variabilidad y cambio climáticos, mediante políticas, programas, herramientas y servicios multisectoriales con enfoque integrado, énfasis en poblaciones y territorios más vulnerables, considerando la gestión integral del agua y de riesgos de desastres, y basados en manejo sostenible de ecosistemas.
ou.name: Pr7.3. Para 2025, las comunidades refuerzan sus estrategias de gestión de riesgos, resiliencia y adaptación al cambio climático basadas en ecosistemas, así como su incidencia con autoridades públicas mediante el diálogo y la participación ciudadana, particularmente de mujeres y jóvenes, contribuyendo a reducir los desplazamientos por motivos climáticos y desastres.
ou.description:
Subproductos:

7.3.1	Al 2022, las comunidades cuentan con capacidades fortalecidas, herramientas para generar inclusiva y participativamente planes en materia de resiliencia y adaptación al cambio climático, integrando la adaptación basada en ecosistemas e incluyendo específicamente a los sistemas de conocimientos locales y tradicionales de los pueblos indígenas y las comunidades afromexicanas, preparándose ante eventos climáticos extremos y la transformación gradual del clima.  

7.3.2	Al 2022, las comunidades, se benefician de herramientas y mecanismos que aseguran su incidencia y colaboración con autoridades, contribuyendo en el diseño, implementación y monitoreo de programas y estrategias ambientales, bajo el enfoque integrado.

ou.parentName: ED7. Al 2025, el Edo. mexicano refuerza sus capacidades de adaptación y resiliencia frente a la variabilidad y cambio climáticos, mediante políticas, programas, herramientas y servicios multisectoriales con enfoque integrado, énfasis en poblaciones y territorios más vulnerables, considerando la gestión integral del agua y de riesgos de desastres, y basados en manejo sostenible de ecosistemas.
ou.name: Pr7.4. Al 2025, las instituciones gubernamentales han fortalecido sus capacidades para una recuperación resiliente en entornos urbanos y rurales, basado en la evidencia, con énfasis en atender las necesidades de los grupos de población y territorios más vulnerables.
ou.description:
Subproductos:

7.4.1	Al 2022, las instituciones gubernamentales estatales y municipales se benefician de mecanismos articulación y herramientas para garantizar el acceso al agua y saneamiento en entornos urbanos y rurales con altas condiciones de vulnerabilidad, contribuyendo a la implementación de medidas de higiene, así como a reducir la propagación de diversas enfermedades, incluida la COVID-19.

7.4.2	Al 2022, las instituciones gubernamentales de los tres niveles de gobierno fortalecen sus capacidades y se benefician de instrumentos para brindar a la población energía eléctrica proveniente de fuentes renovables y limpias.

ou.parentName: ED8. Al 2025, el Estado mexicano cuenta con las capacidades institucionales para prevenir y sancionar todas las formas y manifestaciones de violencia, en particular contra las mujeres, niñas y las y los adolescentes, a la vez que garantiza el acceso a servicios de calidad para la debida atención y protección a las víctimas.
ou.name: Pr8.1. Al 2025, las instituciones de procuración e impartición de justicia cuentan con capacidades fortaleidas y herramientas para la investigación y sanción de todas las formas de violencia en favor de grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad, en particular contra las mujeres y niñas.
ou.description:
Subproductos:

8.1.1	Las instituciones de procuración e impartición de justicia cuentan con capacidades más adecuadas para investigar y sancionar casos de violencia en contra de niñas, niños y adolescentes, incluida a quienes se encuentren en situación de movilidad humana.

8.1.2	Las instituciones de procuración e impartición de justicia aumentan sus capacidades de recopilación y uso de información estadística relacionadas con la investigación de todas las formas de violencia y delitos contra las mujeres y niñas, incluida a quienes se encuentren en situación de movilidad humana.

8.1.3	Las instituciones de procuración e impartición de justicia mejoran sus capacidades de detección e investigación de los delitos de tráfico ilícito de migrantes y trata de personas, incluyendo para fines de explotación sexual, especialmente cuando involucra a mujeres, niños, niñas, adolescentes y poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad.

ou.parentName: ED8. Al 2025, el Estado mexicano cuenta con las capacidades institucionales para prevenir y sancionar todas las formas y manifestaciones de violencia, en particular contra las mujeres, niñas y las y los adolescentes, a la vez que garantiza el acceso a servicios de calidad para la debida atención y protección a las víctimas.
ou.name: Pr8.2. Al 2025, las instituciones públicas responsables de la provisión de servicios esenciales y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil han fortalecido sus capacidades y coordinación para prevenir y erradicar todas las formas de violencia y en favor de grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad, en particular contra las mujeres, niños, niñas y adolescentes.
ou.description:
Subproductos:

8.2.1	Las instituciones públicas responsables de la provisión de servicios esenciales en los ámbitos de la salud, procuración de justicia y servicios sociales, así como de la sociedad civil fortalecen sus esquemas de coordinación interinstitucional en materia de prevención de todas las formas de violencia, en especial contra las mujeres, niñas, niños y adolescentes, incluidas a quienes se encuentren en situación de movilidad humana.

8.2.2	Las instituciones públicas responsables de la provisión de servicios esenciales en los ámbitos de la salud, procuración de justicia y servicios sociales así como de la organizaciones de la sociedad civil aumentan sus capacidades de generación y utilización de información estadística e información cualitativa para el diseño de estrategias de prevención de todas las formas de violencia, con énfasis en las mujeres, niñas, niños y adolescentes, incluidas a quienes se encuentren en situación de movilidad humana

8.2.3	Las instituciones públicas responsables de la provisión de servicios esenciales en los ámbitos de la salud, procuración de justicia y servicios sociales, así como de la sociedad civil desarrollan estrategias integrales de prevención situacional y participación comunitaria para la prevención de todas las formas de violencia, en particular contra las mujeres, niñas, niños y adolescentes, incluidas a quienes se encuentren en situación de movilidad humana.

8.2.4	Las instituciones de procuración e impartición de justicia cuentan con mecanismos adecuados que promuevan, al interior de sus estructuras y en los contenidos que publican o difunden, una vida libre de violencia, en particular contra las mujeres, niños, niñas y adolescentes, con pertinencia lingüística y cultural.

ou.parentName: ED9. Al 2025, instituciones del Estado mexicano y la sociedad civil se encuentran articuladas y con capacidades instaladas para prevenir, denunciar y sancionar actos de corrupción, promover mecanismos de rendición de cuentas y garantizar la participación social y política en la toma de decisiones inclusivas, de manera transparente, en condiciones de igualdad y sin dejar a nadie atrás.
ou.name: Pr9.1. Al 2025, las instituciones de gobierno encargadas de atender denuncias, investigar o sancionar cualquier acto de corrupción, así como de garantizar el derecho al acceso a la información, rendición de cuentas, velar por el manejo efectivo de los recursos, y promover la transparencia han fortalecido sus capacidades, en línea con la Convención de las Naciones Unidas contra la Corrupción.
ou.description:
Subproductos:

9.1.1	Las instituciones de gobierno fortalecen sus protocolos institucionales y mejoran sus capacidades y coordinación para prevenir, identificar y gestionar riesgos de corrupción, promoviendo la integridad, y previniendo conflictos de interés en el ámbito de las contrataciones públicas y adquisiciones.  

9.1.2	Las instituciones de gobierno de nivel local conocen y cuentan con recomendaciones para mejorar el marco normativo y los programas anticorrupción en materia de contratación y gestión de la hacienda pública, información pública y protección a denunciantes, de acuerdo con los principios de la Convención de las Naciones Unidas contra la Corrupción.

9.1.3	Las instituciones de gobierno responsables de prevenir y combatir la corrupción cuentan con capacidades fortalecidas y herramientas, desde el enfoque integrado, para desarrollar estrategias de prevención del lavado de dinero y recuperación de activos producto de la corrupción.

9.1.4	Las instituciones de gobierno a nivel local cuentan con herramientas para prevenir la corrupción, garantizar el acceso a la información, la participación ciudadana y la rendición de cuentas en sus estrategias y programas.

9.1.5	Las instituciones deportivas del sector público y privado fortalecen sus protocolos institucionales y mejoran sus capacidades y coordinación para prevenir, identificar y gestionar riesgos de corrupción, promoviendo la integridad, y previniendo conflictos de interés en el sector deporte.

ou.parentName: ED9. Al 2025, instituciones del Estado mexicano y la sociedad civil se encuentran articuladas y con capacidades instaladas para prevenir, denunciar y sancionar actos de corrupción, promover mecanismos de rendición de cuentas y garantizar la participación social y política en la toma de decisiones inclusivas, de manera transparente, en condiciones de igualdad y sin dejar a nadie atrás.
ou.name: Pr9.2. Al 2025, las organizaciones de la sociedad civil, las instituciones de gobierno y el sector privado cuentan con herramientas para prevenir la corrupción, así como para garantizar mecanismos relativos a la transparencia y el acceso a la información, la participación ciudadana, la rendición de cuentas, y la gestión pública justa y equitativa.
ou.description:
Subproductos:

9.2.1	Las organizaciones de la sociedad civil y la población beneficiaria de los programas sociales federales, estatales y municipales, aumentan sus capacidades para realizar contraloría social, impulsar la participación ciudadana, la incidencia, la corresponsabilidad, la educación para la integridad y la transversalización del enfoque integrado.  

9.2.2	El sector privado cuenta con herramientas para promover la integridad corporativa, la competencia justa, la corresponsabilidad en la prevención de la corrupción y desarrollar estrategias de prevención, identificación y gestión de riesgos de la corrupción en sus organizaciones. 

9.2.3	El sector privado y el sector académico cuentan con herramientas para fomentar conjuntamente la prevención de la corrupción y la integridad, para fortalecer la conducta, los comportamientos y la capacidad de toma de decisiones ética de juventudes y profesionistas.

9.2.4	Las instituciones especializadas y los funcionarios públicos de los tres niveles de gobierno conocen la importancia de facilitar, de manera proactiva, el acceso a información pública que permita la toma de decisiones informada, que habilite el derecho de acceso a la información y que fortalezca la cultura de la transparencia entre la ciudadanía, especialmente entre los grupos más vulnerables.

ou.parentName: ED10. Al 2025, el Estado mexicano fortalece la promoción, protección y respeto del ejercicio pleno de los derechos humanos y el acceso a la justicia, la verdad y reparación para toda la población, especialmente la población que se encuentra en contextos de mayor vulnerabilidad, en condiciones de igualdad y bajo el principio de no dejar a nadie atrás.
ou.name: Pr10.1. Al 2025, las instituciones públicas de impartición y procuración de justicia y los organismos públicos de derechos humanos cuentan con herramientas para la adopción de normas y estándares internacionales en materia de derechos humanos, acceso a la justicia, tratamiento para el uso indebido de drogas, y acceso a la reparación integral en casos de violaciones graves a derechos humanos y prevención del delito, con perspectiva de género.
ou.description:
Subproductos:

10.1.1	Los medios de comunicación, periodistas, activistas, las personas, mecanismos e instituciones defensoras de derechos humanos conocen buenas prácticas y herramientas para garantizar derechos de protección, reporte y monitoreo, reparación integral, medidas de no repetición, acceso a la información, transparencia y difusión responsable de contenidos, en el marco de sus atribuciones.

10.1.2	Las instituciones públicas de impartición y procuración de justicia mejoran sus capacidades para la atención prioritaria, el acceso a la reparación integral y las medidas de no repetición en casos de violaciones graves a derechos humanos, prevenir la delincuencia y hacer frente a retos como la desaparición de personas, tanto forzada como cometida por particulares, la tortura, tratos crueles e inhumanos, las ejecuciones extrajudiciales, el uso indebido de drogas y la delincuencia organizada, y cuentan con capacidades para diseñar políticas basadas en evidencia, bajo el enfoque integrado, y en un marco de respeto pleno a los derechos humanos y con perspectiva de género. 

10.1.3	Los medios de comunicación, las personas, mecanismos e instituciones defensoras de derechos humanos fortalecen sus capacidades para mejorar el reporte y monitoreo de los casos de asesinatos y ataques contra periodistas, así como la generación de estadísticas desagregadas y representativas de la problemática.

10.1.4	Las instituciones gubernamentales cuentan con programas y/o políticas para la reducción de la oferta y la demanda de drogas ilícitas, y promueven acciones de prevención y tratamiento, en coordinación con la sociedad civil.

10.1.5	El sistema penitenciario mexicano cuenta con estándares que dignifiquen a las personas privadas de su libertad mediante la protección de sus derechos humanos, acciones de reinserción social y profesionalización del personal penitenciario.

ou.parentName: ED10. Al 2025, el Estado mexicano fortalece la promoción, protección y respeto del ejercicio pleno de los derechos humanos y el acceso a la justicia, la verdad y reparación para toda la población, especialmente la población que se encuentra en contextos de mayor vulnerabilidad, en condiciones de igualdad y bajo el principio de no dejar a nadie atrás.
ou.name: Pr10.2. Al 2022, las autoridades de procuración e impartición de justicia cuentan con información apegada a estándares internacionales para la toma de decisiones que permita mejorar su operación y coordinación, eficientar sus procesos y garantizar el acceso a la justicia en condiciones de igualdad, en especial a grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad, bajo el enfoque integrado y con pleno apego a la debida diligencia y al respeto a los derechos humanos.
ou.description:
Subproductos:

10.2.1	Las instituciones de procuración e impartición de justicia incrementan sus capacidades operativas para garantizar que los procesos de investigación de los delitos se apeguen al debido proceso, que haya mecanismos de coordinación y  actuación para garantizar que la procuración e impartición de justicia sea eficiente, expedita y apegada a derechos humanos, y las personas tengan un acceso igualitario a la justicia pronta y expedita, así como a la atención prioritaria, el acceso a la reparación integral y las medidas de no repetición en casos de violaciones graves a derechos humanos.

10.2.2	Las instituciones de procuración e impartición de justicia cuentan con información basada en evidencia para medir el progreso hacia las metas del ODS 16.

10.2.3	Las instituciones de procuración e impartición de justicia mejoran sus capacidades para la prevención, investigación y persecución de delitos graves a los derechos humanos y aquellos vinculados con la delincuencia organizada, como el lavado de dinero, la trata de personas, el tráfico de drogas, el tráfico ilícito de migrantes, o el tráfico de armas; y cuentan con mecanismos que mejoren la asistencia a las víctimas de estos delitos, en particular de niñas, niños, adolescentes y mujeres.

ou.parentName: ED10. Al 2025, el Estado mexicano fortalece la promoción, protección y respeto del ejercicio pleno de los derechos humanos y el acceso a la justicia, la verdad y reparación para toda la población, especialmente la población que se encuentra en contextos de mayor vulnerabilidad, en condiciones de igualdad y bajo el principio de no dejar a nadie atrás.
ou.name: Pr10.3. Al 2025 las instituciones, organizaciones de la sociedad civil y el sector privado que interactúan con personas migrantes, desplazadas, solicitantes de asilo y refugiadas fortalecen sus capacidades para brindar asistencia, protección y apoyo para la integración local y el acceso a la justicia, en línea con los estándares internacionales de derechos humanos.
ou.description:
Subproductos:

10.3.1	Las instituciones gubernamentales que interactúan con personas migrantes, personas desplazadas y refugiadas, organizaciones de la sociedad civil, y el sector privado mejoran su capacidad institucional, así como sus esquemas de coordinación para favorecer la protección de estas poblaciones y garantizar su acceso a derechos.

10.3.2	Las organizaciones de la sociedad civil, instituciones gubernamentales y el sector privado cuentan con herramientas y conocimientos para promover la autonomía y la inclusión de las personas migrantes, personas desplazadas y refugiadas en el tejido productivo y social de las comunidades de acogida a favor del desarrollo local.

sp.name: AXE 1 UNSDCF: GOUVERNANCE EFFICACE ET REDEVABLE POUR UNE SOCIETE EN PAIX, JUSTE ET INCLUSIVE
sp.description: Cet AXE vise  à renforcer les institutions en charge de la justice, favoriser la résolution pacifique des conflits, contribuer à la promotion de l'état de droit et renforcer la démocratie dans le pays.

sp.name: AXE 1 UNSDCF: GOUVERNANCE EFFICACE ET REDEVABLE POUR UNE SOCIETE EN PAIX, JUSTE ET INCLUSIVE
AXE 2 UNSDCF: CROISSANCE INCLUSIVE, RESILIENCE ET DURABILITE ENVIRONNEMENTALE
sp.description: Dans cet AXE il s'agira d'appuyer le processus de formulation et de mise en œuvre d'une stratégie de croissance économique forte et inclusive, avec des politiques sectorielles alignées sur les ODD et mieux articulées avec le cadre macroéconomique et budgétaire de l'Etat, d'accompagner les initiatives gouvernementales d'emplois et de revenus décents pour les personnes vulnérable et de renforcer les résiliences face au changement climatique.

sp.name: AXE 2 UNSDCF: CROISSANCE INCLUSIVE, RESILIENCE ET DURABILITE ENVIRONNEMENTALE
AXE 3 UNSDCF: SERVICES SOCIAUX DE BASE ACCESSIBLE, DE QUALITE, ET PROTECTION SOCIALE INCLUSIVE
sp.description: Dans le cadre de l'axe 3, les Nations Unies contribuent à améliorer l'accès aux services sociaux de base, à  accompagner les efforts du Gouvernement à approfondir la vision et le cadre politique, juridique et financier du système de protection sociale.

sp.name: AXE 3 UNSDCF: SERVICES SOCIAUX DE BASE ACCESSIBLE, DE QUALITE, ET PROTECTION SOCIALE INCLUSIVE

oc.description: Dans cet axe, il s'agit de soutenir la mise en œuvre de la stratégie nationale de réconciliation, renforcer les mécanismes de consolidation de la paix et l'état de droit, promouvoir les moyens traditionnels de gestion de conflit et de lutter contre l'extrémisme violent.

oc.description: Dans cet effet les Nations Unies soutiennent les initiatives gouvernementales  pour améliorer la sante maternelle et infantile, soutenir les efforts en faveur de la nutrition et renforcer le système éducatif.

oc.name: Effet 3.2 : D’ici 2024, Les personnes vulnérables ont un accès amélioré aux services de protection sociale, y compris en contexte humanitaire.

sp.name: SP 1 Inclusive growth and sustainable management of natural resources
sp.description: The UN has identified the importance of increasing resilience of poor and vulnerable people to mitigate shocks whether they be natural or man-made. It is anticipated that under this Outcome, communities and individuals will better deal with environmental and economic hardships. Communities and individuals will also enjoy more inclusive growth resulting from more and better jobs in a more diversified economy.

sp.name: SP 2 Social protection and services
sp.description: The UN has identified strong social protection systems and equitable access to quality social services including water, sanitation, hygiene, health and education as key drivers for the full realization of the SDGs and the objective of the global goals of ‘leaving no one behind’. For real change to occur in the universality of access to these services, a multi-dimensional/multi-layered approach with existing and new partners, challenging the status quo and taking implementation and policy risks will be needed.

sp.name: SP 3 Voice and accountability
sp.description: This priority is multifaceted and strongly anchored in the SDG agenda, ensuring that all the peoples of Mongolia benefit from sustainable development and that the poor and marginalized are reached first. The UN, in partnership with the GoM and other development partners, will work towards the informed participation of the poor and marginalized in the sustainable development agenda while building a greater trust in government institutions and ensuring the representation and meaningful participation of women and young people in policy and decision making. The UN will support Mongolia’s democratic institutions to deliver services with mutual accountability and greater transparency, leading to a more inclusive society where human rights are promoted, protected and realized.

ou.name: Output 1.1.1 - Agricultural production strengthened through the rehabilitation of infrastructure; spearheading new technologies and modern production methods; by providing inputs and services, supporting the development of value chains while linking them to local and international markets
ou.description:
UNIDO to establish a butchers training facility, and a model meat shop, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Food Safety and Halal Food Authority (KPFSHFA) and the Livestock and Dairy Development Department (LDD) food safety labs are being supported. An E-learning platform for Master Trainers has been developed on Good Hygiene Practice (GHP) as well as Good Animal Husbandry Practice (GAHP) for farmers and animal transporters. Upgradation of 30 butcher shops is currently underway.  Capacity building of government counterparts (LDD, KPFS&HFA & LCB) on new technique of dehiding thus improving quality of hides/skins for leather industry through Static Flaying Frame (SFF) and exposure to meat value chain.  Training and capacity building of private sector including feedlot farmers, butchers, meat exporters & processing industry on dehiding technique using SFF and animal/meat traceability.  Training of the private sector on the food safety and hygiene during slaughtering, evisceration, meat cuts, packing & packaging, storage and logistics in temperature controlled environment.  Understanding on feedlot farming business, farm management, preventive measures, animal buying and good husbandry practices to be adopted to improve meat quality and availability.  Initiation of a pilot project on animal and meat traceability starting from farm level through data management at all levels from buying till slaughtering, meat cuts, packaging and retail selling.  Exposure of meat value chain actors in understanding meat export business, International requirements, standards, approvals / certifications and quarantine protocols in meat export at an abattoir engaged in meat export.   Develop market linkages and exposure of private sector to understand high end market requirements and fulfil their food safety protocols and become partner in their economic activity/business. 
UNIDO upgraded and operationalized the only Pesticide Quality Control and Research Laboratory in Balochistan. 767 (358 female & 409 male) farmers have been trained on Good Agriculture Practices (GAP) in seven districts. An E-learning platform on GAP has also been developed for the agriculture department and farmers. The Balochistan PPP platform, established under the PAFAID project, regularly meets to ensure collaboration of stakeholders. The organization of the first-ever apple packaging solution competition among the students of key universities in Balochistan. Training of 17 food inspectors (16 male & 1 female) on “Risk-Based Food Inspection and Food Safety Management Systems” and Good Hygiene Practices from Balochistan Food Authority
Training of 29 (26 male and 3 female) stakeholders and  403 students (162 male and 241) on packaging solutions in collaboration with World Packaging Organization. Assessment of the four businesses/facilities to identify and support potential for capacity building, improved food safety practices and new value adding technologies for apple processing. The project has initiated a competition on the implementation of good agriculture practices among the apple farmers in the seven districts of Balochistan. The purpose of the competition is to assess the implementation the good agriculture practices by the farmers who were trained on GAP by the master trainers.

ou.name: Output 1.1.5 - Strengthened capacities of public and private sector entities to implement policies and plans in the field of energy efficiency and renewable energy through promotion of new mechanisms for advancing solar, biomass and other renewable energy technologies, such as introducing business-to-business (B2B) models in the private sector
ou.description:
Policy Recommendations for the promotion of Renewable Energy  & Energy Efficiency developed and handed over to NEECA and AEDB. Published reports on Sectoral Analysis of Energy Intensive Sectors and Analytical report to summarize the energy-saving data from all Energy Efficiency Interventions in 50 industrial sectors. A forward approach has been taken to cover energy assessments and the implementation of the EnMS based on ISO 50001-2018 in 50 selected industrial units. Overall 800+ different capacity-building trainings were conducted to enhance the knowledge and skills of professionals and young entrepreneurs which includes more than 100 young women energy professionals, trained in 20 different types of training stretched over one day to three days. Special grants were provided to 11 industrial units that were interested in ISO 5001 certification and needed financial push for energy optimization investments. 11 Industries have successfully completed the ISO 50001:2018 certification. Other industries are working on the implementation and certification of ISO 50001. Building the capacity of public and private sectors. During the implementation of EnMS, around 20 industry professionals have been trained and received lead auditor certifications on ISO 50001:2018. In the project’s concluding phase 11 Webinars and 4 Workshops were organized to disseminate learning of the projects related to EnMS and RE& EE to other industries that were not part of the project. A total of 12 success stories were drafted to highlight the impact of the project including the portfolio of implementation of EnMS/SO and deployment of RE. the document also illustrates the mandate of UNIDO i.e., Inclusive and Sustainable Industrial Development ensured across the project. Out of the 20 training, two specialized training sessions were on Certified Energy Manager (CEM) and Certified Energy Auditors (CEA). Special grants were provided to 11 industrial units that were interested in ISO 5001 certification and needed financial push for energy optimization investments.11 Industries have successfully completed the ISO 50001:2018 certification. Other industries are working on the implementation and certification of ISO 50001.Building the capacity of public and private sectors. During the implementation of EnMS, around 20 industry professionals have been trained and received lead auditor certifications on ISO 50001:2018. 
In the project’s concluding phase 11 Webinars and 4 Workshops were organized to disseminate learning of the projects related to EnMS and RE& EE to other industries that were not part of the project. A total of 12 success stories were drafted to highlight the impact of the project including the portfolio of implementation of EnMS/SO and deployment of RE. the document also illustrates the mandate of UNIDO i.e., Inclusive and Sustainable Industrial Development ensured across the project.  Upscaling RE investments in the industrial sector through developing partnerships with industries for implementing RE projects of a capacity of 12+ MWs for captive power purposes. Grants are provided for the implementation of RE projects in industries. 
6+ MW of Solar PV Projects have been completed based on the B2B model;
 5+ MW of PV captive power plants installed at different industrial units;
 1+ MW RE projects in support of small businesses and micro-enterprises including women-owned enterprises for productive uses;
Collaborated with the National Rural Support Program (NRSP) for Renewable Energy Investment Projects. UNIDO has achieved and exceeded the target, by installing 1.3 MW RE projects cumulatively instead of the target of 600 KW. That includes 474 beneficiaries together with 21 women-owned enterprises.
The Energy Desk has been established in collaboration with SMEDA with the prime objective to provide a one-window platform to facilitate the promotion of RE and EE technologies and investments in small and medium enterprises in Pakistan. The primary aim of the Energy Desk is to counsel and guide SMEs regarding the adoption of EE and RE technologies and provide information on market players including service providers, technology suppliers, financing facilities options, and regulatory updates. As a successful pilot scheme, UNIDO’s Energy Performance Awards have set a platform for a regular national-level event to motivate the industrial sector to contribute toward a sustainable, clean, and green Pakistan. Besides from an initiative taken by UNIDO by introducing AEE USA Certification courses like CEA and CEM at the local level, the professional who attended the courses, worked to set a  local chapter of the Association of Energy Engineers (AEE). UNIDO project team members, took active participation and also become key office holders (honorary basis) to align this chapter with project activities. The chapter is conducting regular webinars/training on RE/EE-related subjects and providing advisory services to local professional.

ou.name: Output 4.1.1 - Integrated and multi-sectoral ‘National and Provincial Nutrition’ policies, strategies and initiatives are developed and implemented including enhanced public financial allocations in line with provincial priorities including sustained momentum of Scaling UP Nutrition (SUN) interventions across Pakistan.
ou.description:
WFP provided technical support to SUN secretariat and SUN units in Balochistan and Sindh. Due to Nation wide emergency Nutrition markers  exercise is delayed in some areas. The process for the development of a costed multi sectoral national nutrition action plan with provincial roadmap contributed to increased capacity for planning, coordination, monitoring and strengthening of multi-sectoral nutrition programming. Public financing for nutrition remains a challenge, however some funds for the Accelerated Action Plan for stunting reduction programme (AAP) in Sindh, and Procurement of Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) were allocated by the Government of  Sindh and Punjab Provinces.  

Coordination mechanisms and Technical Working Groups providing a platform for multisectoral coordination on Early Childhood Development were established in each province to engage across education, child protection, health, and nutrition sectors with support from UNICEF.    

Public financial allocation reviews are institutionalized for annual development plans through the SUN platform with UNICEF's technical support, to understand the level and division of financial allocation for nutrition-specific and -sensitive interventions in over one thousand public sector annual development plans in PAK, GB, Punjab and KP. Knowledge on public financial allocation is used to systematically advocate for increased investment in nutrition-sensitive interventions.

Integrated CMAM programme for the moderate malnutrition was implemented in 14 districts of KP and AJK. Around 78000 beneficiaries receives nutrition support.
WHO established 11 NSC in 2022 in Sindh and Balochistan, 38 NSCs strengthened across Pakistan and provided therapeutic milk to 11 New and 38 strengthened NSCs. In trainings on BFHI,  40 medical officers and 20 Nurses trained from Islamabad and KPK.

33.4 million children 6-59 months old were provided two doses of Vitamin A in 2022, with supply support from UNICEF.
Although there are large number of severly wasted children yet to be reached, a total of 323,032 children (146,176 boys and 176,856 girls) were admitted for treatment of severe wasting. Multiple micronutrient supplemention provided to 822,231 children (409,340 boys and 412,891 girls) and IFA supplementation to 1,789,507 mothers and 522,000 adolescent in 2022, for which UNICEF provided technical support in capacity building.             

Provincial implementation plans for the Maternal and Adolescent Nutrition Strategy were developed with UNICEF's support, and approved by provincial and national Governments. The strategy was lauched in Balochistan, Sindh and Gilgit-Balchistan, while launch in the remaining provinces and implementation will commence in 2023.

ou.description: In order to generate more employment across various sectors, a new Economic Development Plan for KP was developed by UNDP, which has now been approved by the KP Chief Minister [E70].Further, in an effort to decrease unemployment, UNDP trained 2,480 youth (men 1,696 and women 784) in different industrial trades, 223 (men 151, women 72) in eco-tourism e-commerce, and another 410 (men 243, women 159, transgenders 8) in social entrepreneurs under SDG bootcamp funded by JAZZ [E71]. Out of these, 1,238 (boys 866, girls 372) are working [E72]. In collaboration with the KP Tourism Department, UNDP trained, 210 youths (68 women) around Eco Tourism and E-Commerce (Dir and Swat) where potential for E-commerce and Eco Tourism is imminent [E73IRRF3.3.1]. UNDP in Balochistan enhanced the capacity of marginalized youth (280 including 90 women) and trained them in different technical and vocational trades enhancing the potential of Small-Scale Supplier [E74][IRRF3.3.1]. To enhance economic growth opportunities, UNDP initiated process for increasing access of Medium, Small, and Micro Entrepreneurs (MSMEs) and youth in North Waziristan, South Waziristan, and Khyber district to formal financing. UNDP (through its responsible party; iConsult) has started engagement with potential commercial banks to extend their services in the project districts and develop products that could attract the MSMEs and youth for business purpose [E75][EA2.2.1].Under WASH IWP priority area, to support the Balochistan Government, UNDP initiated renovation and repair work of hospitals and schools in 2 districts (Nushki and Killa Abdullah) and five out of 29 schemes (schools and hospitals) have been completed [E69.1][IRRF3.2.2].  In KP, for improved livelihood, construction and rehabilitation of WASH services in 82 market hubs and 02 water filtration plants were initiated [E76], with an aim to bring more clients to the markets.

ou.description:
For protection of people especially in the northern zones prone to natural hazards UNDP enhanced the capacity of national and provincial disaster management authorities through formulation of several policies and actions plans related to climate change and adaptation and disaster risk reduction (DRR). This included updating of National Climate Change Policy (draft in 2021), Nationally determined Contributions (NDCs) (2021), and Climate Change Action Plans at the provincial level (2021). In collaboration with Capital Development Authority, Under the waste management initiative, 19,371 people (including 9104 women) got access to improved waste management system in two sectors of Islamabad. 200 sanitary staff (35 women, 165 men) received training on waste collection and segregation, 33 sets (120 Litres bins) of 3 bins system were also installed and 51 yellow-colored bins were also distributed in the target sectors. During the year, 5 low-cost plastic recycling solutions were also formulated by different academic institutions through UNESCO and the Pakistan Science Foundation to transform plastic into products like plastic and filaments that can be used in 3D printers. UNDP also provided 45 benches made from recycled plastics and handed over these benches to Capital Development Authority and Senate of Pakistan[E83][IRRF 4.1.1].

Further UNDP’s capacity building initiatives enabled the district disaster response teams to conduct independent early recovery needs assessments of early recovery of people in emergency. UNDP assisted the governments of Sindh and KP to save people from risks of climate change through formulating landscape management plans. Similarly with the same aim it aided the government of KP by providing a management information system for forest monitoring resulting in effective forest management.   
In 2022, for enhanced climate resilience of people of Pakistan, UNDP supported development and finalization of two Climate Change Adaptation Action Plans (CCAAPs) for GB and KP, which have been adopted by the respective provincial Governments and being used to address and mitigate GLOF risks and adverse impacts of climate change. 
For effective disaster preparedness and mitigation of public at large, KP and GB has been supported by UNDP to develop four plans (02 monsoon and 02 winter contingency) [E65-E65.5][EA 4.2.3]. 
In 2021, with support of UNDP Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) were updated and submitted to UNFCCC by the government of Pakistan.

Once it is installed, will benefit 100 percent population of 24 valleys to cope with potential disaster of GLOF (IRRF 3.1.2) [E78]. ou.name: Output 9.1.1 - Democratic governance of 'State' institutions, including 'Parliament', 'Provincial Assemblies', 'Local Governments' and 'Electoral Management Bodies' (EMBs) strengthened to be transparent, accountable and responsive to citizens' needs for improved service delivery (UNDP/UNODC)
ou.description:
UNDP undertook national level voter education campaign for enhanced awareness of public for upcoming general elections. UNDP support to Election Commission of Pakistan comprised of technical and professional skills of 1,377 officers (1160 men, 217 women) 21 ECP officers (19 men 3 women) [E33]; testing and development of elections monitoring system [E34]; support for research and development structure, staffing plan, draft roadmap for Internet Voting System (IVS)[E35]. To ensure free and fair elections, UNDP educated youth voters (3,237=1,683 women and 1,554 men) in universities, and colleges while 1,163 stakeholders (37 women and 1,126 men) were engaged through sessions held with media, local communities, Civil Society in KP, Balochistan[E18]. UNDP supported voter education campaigns through multiple media sources for Local Government Elections in KP (18.181m reached for phase II), Balochistan (6.8m) and Sindh (44.03m) [E18][EA1.1.1].

To support parliament in election reforms act 2017, UNDP arranged extensive consultations (amendment bill 2021). The bill has reached for debate in the Parliament [E36] [IRRF 2.4.1EA 1.1.1]. 

 UNDP has supported over 40 stakeholder engagements of Home and Tribal Affairs Department (HTAD) KP and district administrations which led to improved service delivery mechanisms in merged area border communities [E32.1-E32.4][IRRF 1.1.1]. UNDP’s explored key factors behind delayed recruitment for top-level vacancies (Executive Recruitment in Public Sector Organizations) and developed a recruitment manual for Ministry to expedite their recruitment process. 

For improved health service delivery, UNDP supported the national and provincial AIDS control programmers (ACPs), to treat HIV positive patients (16,782 women 45,470 men) with anti-retroviral therapy (ART) against HIV [E08][IRRF1.4.1].

ou.name: Output 9.1.2 - Efficiency, effectiveness and responsiveness of the 'Rule of Law' institutions improved for timely, affordable and accessible provision of justice services (UNDP/UNODC/UNWOMEN,UNICEF)
ou.description:
With UNDP’s support Merged Areas’ have their first ever Policing Plans [E40-E40.7] [IRRF2.2.1] for effective law enforcement in the area. KP police has a public outreach strategy which is helping KP Police to know it’s public perception and positioning[E41][IRRF2.2.1].Women participation in provincial legal profession in KP, has been encouraged through UNDP’s stipends and scholarships for law students [E42] [IRRF2.2.3: EA 1.2.1]. 

Through provision of 35 virtual courts and 75 virtual points and linking of Peshawar High Court through this facility with prisons has increased the case disposal rate [E43][IRRF2.2.3EA 1.2.1]. To make informal justice mechanisms more efficient in KP/MAs, UNDP supported the revision of Dispute Resolution Councils (DRC) Rules under KP Police Act 2017 [E44] and for formal justice mechanisms included technical support to Balochistan High Court for development of court-annexed mediation rules under section 89-A, Civil Procedure Court 1908, to ensure simpler and affordable legal solutions for the people [E45][IRRF2.2.1]
With support of UNDP, Balochistan judiciary has operational ADR mechanism and adopted courts annexed rules under section 89-A [E46]. Whereas KP has revised ‘KP Prison and Act rules’ while leading to improved conditions of the inmates[E47-E48-E49][IRRF 2.2.1]. 

With UNDP’s support Peshawar based KP Forensic Science Laboratory was operationalized and Service and Operations Rules under the 2020 Act were developed [E25] a great step towards speedy prosecution investigations in the province. 

UNDP enhanced access to justice through establishing the Provincial Justice Committee (PJC) Secretariate at PHC which is closely coordinating with the District Criminal Justice Coordination Committees (CJCCs) [IRRF 2.2.1]. UNDP supported Ministry of Human Rights in developing a strategy for harmonizing human rights data collection mechanisms [E51] while complementing the implementation of Pakistan’s National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights.

ou.name: Output 9.1.3 - Through active citizens engagement, public policy priorities shaped by national/provincial governments, planning, financing and monitoring mechanisms established, statistical capacities of core governing institutions strengthened, facilitating implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (UNDP/UNFPA/UNHABITAT/UNICEF/WHO)
ou.description:
UNDP’s technical support to the government to shape priority policy areas continued in 2022. 

A joint ‘SDG Investment Report 2021’ was published in partnership with the government on Financing for Development and nature capital solutions [E54][EA1.3.1]. Additionally following interventions were undertaken such as portfolio presentations at global investment platforms such as the SDG Investment Fairs and ESCAP’s Asia Pacific Forum [E55][EA1.3.1]; launch of the SDG Investments and Climate Financing Facility, development of high-impact SDG-aligned value propositions for private sector investment [E06] [EA1.3.1]. A diagnostic report on Inclusive Insurance and Risk Financing in Pakistan was published [E56]; countrywide consultations on Disaster Risk Financing solutions [E57] have created buy-in from the Balochistan and Sindh governments to develop Insurance and Risk Financing solutions in their provinces [E58 and E58.1] [E.A 1.1.1]. 
Gender Training Assessments resulted in capacity-building trainings for government stakeholders all over Pakistan [E60]. To improve planning under SDG localization efforts, UNDP prepared frameworks for key priority sectors like social protection, health, and education at the sub-national level, such as district development plans and SDG frameworks, as well as documentation and Situation Analysis Reports on SDG 2, 4, 6 and 7 [E62][E.A 1.3.2] serving as baseline for future planning. UNDP has increased the citizens engagement by engaging the academia on the topic “Reimagining Resilience: the Transition to Sustainable Cities” [E16], and a report was also jointly launched on 'Migration, Livelihoods & Resilience in Karachi: A Study on Social Cohesion and Informal Urban Settlements' [E64].

ou.description: ONU Mujeres participó técnicamente de la creación de la Ley 431 del 25 de abril de 2024, que establece el marco normativo para el cuidado en el país. Desde una mirada integral, la ley comprende el cuidado desde todas las etapas de vida de una persona (primera infancia, adultez y tercera edad) y a las personas con discapacidad. La ley reconoce le cuidado como un derecho y pone un especial énfasis en las mujeres que realizan trabajos de cuidado de forma no remunerada.

sp.description:
Harnessing the UN's reputation as an impartial steward of Bougainville peace processes, the project aims to
support leaders, parliamentarians, officials and communities in PNG, and especially the Autonomous Region in Bougainville, to further
progress ongoing post-Referendum negotiations and related peace processes at the national and regional levels and to ensure that
diverse community members' voices are included in those processes. The project will also support a number of peace-supporting
economic development initiatives aimed at increasing opportunities for women and other marginalized groups to participate in the
formal economy, targeting those communities which had been particularly affected by the consequences of the Bougainville conflict
and in alignment with the existing Bougainville innovation hubs.

oc.description: With the aim to ensure that underwater cultural heritage is identified, protected and sustainably managed in the Pacific, this activity will aim to raise awareness and promote the ratification and effective implementation of the 2001 Convention in Papua New Guinea. The activities will include the elaboration of a gap analysis and national interest analysis that will inform the development of an online training suite of curated informative material. The tailored policy advice will aim to provide a better understanding of the UCH Convention in terms of its benefits and implications in PNG within the framework of overall capacity building for the UCH safeguarding for sustainable development.

sp.name: Prioridad estratégica 1 - Desarrollo social/personas
sp.description: Esta prioridad estratégica busca apoyar a Paraguay a: reducir las desigualdades e incrementar el acceso a servicios sociales de calidad y la protección de todas las personas, con el fin de asegurar su inclusión social, mejorar su calidad de vida, garantizar los derechos humanos y alcanzar la igualdad de género.

sp.name: Prioridad estratégica 2 - Sostenibilidad ambiental/planeta
sp.description: Esta prioridad estratégica busca apoyar a: El Estado, los actores económicos, sociales y la población en general a modificar su relación con el medio ambiente, adoptando estilos de vida y patrones de consumo y producción que permitan avanzar hacia el desarrollo sostenible.

sp.name: Prioridad estratégica 3 - Desarrollo económico inclusivo/prosperidad
sp.description: Esta prioridad estratégica busca apoyar a Paraguay a fin de que cuente con una matriz productiva diversificada, con instituciones, normas y políticas que promuevan un desarrollo sostenible e inclusivo, basado en la innovación y articulación intersectorial, con énfasis en el sistema educativo y productivo.

sp.name: Prioridad estratégica 4 - Fortalecimiento institucional/paz y justicia
sp.description: Esta prioridad estratégica tiene como fin apoyar a que Paraguay cuente con instituciones fortalecidas, articuladas, transparentes, con mecanismos de participación ciudadana que promuevan la representatividad de diversos grupos, con mejoras en los accesos a la justicia y seguridad, y una población con sólidas capacidades para el ejercicio de sus derechos democráticos.

oc.description:

 - Continued political will, peace, and security necessary for investor confidence.

sp.name: People — According to the principles of ‘Leave No One Behind’ (LNOB), ensure that all human beings can fulfil their potential in dignity, equity, and equality in a healthy environment (SDGs 1–5)
sp.description: The achievement of SDG/SDR indicators that correspond to SDG/SDR 1 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. The SDG/SDR 2 indicators prevalence of undernourishment and cereal yield have been achieved. The SDG/SDR 3 indicators maternal mortality rate, neonatal mortality rate, mortality rate, under-five mortality rate, incidence of tuberculosis, adolescent fertility rate, births attended by skilled health personnel, surviving infants who received two WHO-recommended vaccines, and subjective well-being have been achieved. The SDG/SDR 4 indicators net primary enrolment rate, lower secondary completion rate, and literacy rate have been achieved. No SDG/SDR 5 indicators have been reported in the data as achieved as of 2021.

sp.name: Prosperity — Ensure that all human beings can enjoy prosperous and fulfilling lives (SDGs 7–11)
sp.description: The SDG/SDR 7 indicators population with access to electricity and population with access to clean fuels and technology for cooking have been achieved. No SDG/SDR 8 indicators have been achieved as of 2021. The SDG/SDR 9 indicators population using the internet, mobile broadband subscriptions, Logistics Performance Index: quality of trade and transport-related infrastructure, and Times Higher Education Universities Ranking: average score of top 3 universities have been achieved. The achievement of SDG/SDR 10 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. No SDG/SDR 11 indicators have been achieved as of 2021 as per available data. No SDG/SDR indicators that correspond to SDGs 7 or 8 face major challenges as of 2021. The SDG/SDR 9 indicator that faces major challenges is expenditure on research and development. The assessment of SDG/SDR 10 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. The SDG/SDR 11 indicator that faces major challenges is annual mean concentration of particulate matter of less than 2.5 microns in diameter.

sp.description:
6264 entrepreneurs, (92% women), have been trained on financial literacy and have benefited from business development skills training, business coaching/mentorship, and access to finance, all aimed improving business and economic opportunities for the women entrepreneurs and their households.  
2975 of the entrepreneurs trained are linked to finance services and more than 828 have benefited from loans to grow their businesses. 314 have had their businesses formalized.

oc.parentName: Serbia harnesses the full potential of a green, sustainable and inclusive economy
oc.name: 1.1  Serbia adopts and implements climate change and environmentally friendly strategies that increase community resilience, decrease carbon footprint and amplify the benefits of national investments
oc.description:
•	Serbia shifts its energy consumption to be more affordable, efficient and promote renewables
•	Cities implement clean air strategies as part of urban development
•	Infrastructure norms and standards mainstream climate change and resilience 
•	Communities have increased resilience to climate induced and human-made disasters

oc.parentName: Serbia harnesses the full potential of a green, sustainable and inclusive economy
oc.name: 1.2  Natural and Cultural Resources are managed in a sustainable way
oc.description:
•	Serbia protects ecosystems, natural resources and biodiversity 
•	Institutions and communities manage cultural and historical resources to optimize long-term social and economic benefits to all

oc.parentName: Serbia harnesses the full potential of a green, sustainable and inclusive economy
oc.name: 1.3 Equitable economic and employment opportunities are promoted through innovation
oc.description:
•	Local development strategies adopt an area-based approach
•	A greater share of economic activities transition towards circularity: changing how we produce, consume and trade
•	Science, technology, and innovation benefit men and women equally
•	People have access to more decent job opportunities and fair competitive trade

oc.parentName: Well-being, social equity and the human potential are at the heart of systems, policies and practices
oc.name: 2.1.  Universal and inclusive access to quality health, social and protection services is improved
oc.description:
•	More people benefit from universal health coverage, including mental health, drug abuse prevention, and healthier lifestyles
•	Expanded and innovative social care services are supported to ensure improved living conditions 
•	State institutions and CSOs ensure effective prevention and improved access to gender sensitive quality services for survivors of violence, exploitation and abuse

oc.parentName: Well-being, social equity and the human potential are at the heart of systems, policies and practices
oc.name: 2.2.  Skills, education and capabilities are enhanced to ensure equitable outcomes for all
oc.description:
•	Formal education (incl. TVET) becomes a key enabler for leaving no one behind
•	More people access informal education, life skills and life-long learning including digital literacy 
•	Women and girls’ empowerment and skills development lead to equitable access to economic and political opportunities

oc.parentName: Well-being, social equity and the human potential are at the heart of systems, policies and practices
oc.name: 2.3 Mobility and demographic transition become vectors for positive change and prosperity for all people
oc.description:
•	Capacities of national and local stakeholders are strengthened to develop and implement evidence-based development and population policies
•	Migration outcomes are improved through mobility of skills, knowledge and capacities
•	People across generations benefit from strengthened community cohesion and cultural connections

oc.parentName: Building trust and mutual accountability through the Rule of Law, Rights and Duties agenda
oc.name: 3.1.  All people, especially the more vulnerable, benefit from the realization of human rights, gender equality and enhanced rule of law in line with international commitments
oc.description:
•	National and local authorities, including the judicial system, are supported in policymaking and implementation that guarantees rights for all 
•	Oversight and independent bodies are strengthened in their monitoring and reporting
•	Institutional and operational capacities in the area of home affairs are strengthened

oc.parentName: Building trust and mutual accountability through the Rule of Law, Rights and Duties agenda
oc.name: 3.2.  All people benefit from effective governance and meaningful civic engagement
oc.description:
•	Governance systems for planning, budgeting, and monitoring of national and local development are more efficient and SDG focused
•	Civic engagement and representation are enhanced for the benefit of society 
•	Emergency preparedness and response guarantees that all lives are equal
•	Regional and transborder cooperation, security, and trust building are enhanced

sp.name: Priorité stratégique 1 - Résultat Stratégique 1: Développement du Capital Humain
sp.description:
Ce résultat stratégique sur le développement du capital humain contribue à l’Axe n°4 « Amélioration de la qualité de vie de la population tchadienne » du PND et s’inscrit dans l’agenda 2030 sous les ODD 3, 4, 6, 10, 11, et 17. Il compte plus d’agences des Nations Unies qui participent à sa mise en œuvre que les deux autres résultats stratégiques, notamment : UNICEF, PAM, HCR, UNESCO, OCHA et OIM (contribuant à l’effet 1) ; PNUD, UNICEF, OMS, ONUSIDA, HCR, PAM, UNFPA (contribuant à l’effet 2) ; et y a que HCR, UNICEF et OIM (contribuant à l’effet 3.)
Cependant, par rapport aux autres résultats stratégiques de l’UNDAF, : le ministère de l’Education Nationale et de la Promotion Civique, le ministère de la Femme, de la Famille et de la Protection de la Petite Enfance, le ministère de la Santé publique et de la solidarité nationale, le ministère de l’Environnement et de la pèche, le ministère de l’Economie, de la planification du développement et de la coopération internationale.

sp.name: Priorité stratégique 2 - Résultat Stratégique 2. Protection sociale, gestion des crises et durabilité
sp.description: Ce résultat stratégique 2 « Protection sociale, gestion de crise et durabilité environnementale» contribue à trois des axes du Plan National de Développement, notamment  à l’Axe n°2 « renforcement des bases de la bonne Gouvernance et de l’Etat de droit » , à l’Axe n°3 « Une économie diversifiée et compétitive » et  à l’Axe n°4 « Amélioration de la qualité de vie de la population tchadienne » et s’inscrit dans l’agenda 2030 sous les ODD  1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, 11, 13, 15, et 17. Sept agences des Nations Unies (FAO,  HCR, OCHA,  OIM,  PAM,  UNFPA et UNICEF) participent à sa mise en œuvre avec la collaboration de six ministères, à savoir, Ministère de la Femme ; Ministère de l’Irrigation et l’équipement agricole ; Ministère de l’Elevage et de la production animale ; Ministère de l’environnement, de l’eau et des pêches ; Ministère de l’administration du territoire ; Ministère l’économie de la Planification du développement et de la coopération internationale.

oc.parentName: Growth of high-potential manufacturing and service sectors, with a focus on innovation, low carbon technologies, technology transfer, sustainable finance, and skills development while promoting natural resource management and environmental sustainability.
oc.name: Thailand’s transformation into an inclusive economy based on green, resilient, low-carbon, sustainable development is accelerated.
oc.description:
The first strategic outcome that is being considered contributes to the NESDP priorities aiming at ‘Targeted Manufacturing and Service Sectors’ and ‘Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability’ to support climate action, biodiversity conservation and disaster management. To focus the UN’s support towards the attainment of this outcome, the UN will collaborate with the
Government and development partners to deliver on the following two focus areas, which contributes to ten of the milestones prioritized in the draft 13th plan: 
- Green growth 
- Resilient community/society

oc.parentName: Human capital development and digital transformation & inclusion as key enablers that will drive Thailand's transformation towards a more sustainable, innovative, inclusive and resilient future
oc.name: Human capital needed for social and inclusive development is improved through strengthening of institutions, partnerships and the empowerment of people.
oc.description:
The second strategic outcome for consideration contributes to the NESDP priorities enhancing Thailand’s human capital. The underlying premise is that people represent the true wealth of the nation. A healthy, well-educated and skilled population, evidenced through the high human development index and based on the foundation of being able to access and exercise human rights, is a good in itself. It will act as a catalyst that drives the transformation of Thailand. The enabling environment for such a transformation is also dependent on the ability of public institutions, systems and services to successfully frame and implement a coherent integrated policy framework, based on principles of equity, accountability, transparency and efficiency. To affect such a change and achieve the impact required, public services need to concentrate on measures that drive standards and outcomes upwards through a focus on quality improvement. To focus the UN’s support on the attainment of this outcome, the UN will collaborate with the Government and development partners including civil society, businesses and communities to prioritize two focus areas, which contribute to nine of the milestones prioritized in the draft 13th Plan. 
- Human capital development through enhancing access to quality of public services,
- Digital inclusion and transformation

oc.parentName: Promote socio-economic opportunity and equity for all citizens to create a more inclusive and prosperous society, where everyone has access to the resources and opportunities they need to achieve their full potential
oc.name: People living in Thailand, especially those at risk of being left furthest behind, are able to participate in and benefit from development, free from all forms of discrimination.
oc.description: The aspiration to leave no one behind is the touchstone of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Women and LGBTI people in particular lag behind their male counterparts across much of Thailand’s social, economic and political life. The energy and dynamism of young people will play a key role in catalysing Thailand’s enterprising culture in the post-COVID-19 landscape. Equally, older people should experience healthy and active aging, as Thailand is an ageing society. Ethnic populations and people living in rural and remote areas should have equal opportunity to those residing in urban areas. Evidence consistently shows the criminalization, stigma, discrimination and other human rights violations towards people infected and affected by HIV reduce service uptake and increase HIV infection. As already noted, the digital divide, nationality as well as status can hold populations back from benefitting and contributing towards Thailand’s collective development journey. In short, where barriers to inclusion and development exist, they need to be systematically dismantled and replaced with enabling opportunities and services.

sp.name: Priority A: People centred governance and rule of law
sp.description: Support to implement practical governance reforms for more effective and transparent public administration, based on Turkmenistan’s international commitments and standards for the rule of law, human rights, gender equality, labour rights, and anti-corruption. More robust and responsive decision-making processes for the delivery of public services, management of the natural resources, economic and public finance management, business regulation that are transparent and fair, using to the extent possible digital systems will be promoted. Cooperation Framework will also support the GoT in improving quality and disaggregation of data for developing more evidence-based and people-centered policies and services.

sp.name: Priority B. Inclusive, green, and sustainable economic growth
sp.description: Implement policy and regulatory reforms creating conditions for stronger economic development in the non-hydrocarbon sectors of the economy, introduce improved banking and financial services and incentives that increase private sector competitiveness and trade, business development and the creation of decent, formal sector jobs. Complementary to this, strengthen climate adaptation and mitigation measures, striving for a more rational use of scarce natural resources and enhanced disaster risk reduction, preparedness and response. Recognizing that hydrocarbon development will continue to play a major part of economic growth, identify important synergies available between hydrocarbon-development, climate change adaptation and mitigation, green technology and jobs. This will support increased resilience and the shift towards sustainable consumption and production and the greening of the economy .

sp.name: Priority C: Quality, inclusive, and affordable health, education, and social protection systems
sp.description: Strengthen performance of the education and skilling system in Turkmenistan which is instrumental to the achievement of the economic growth and diversification goals of the NPSD and PPSD; focus on efforts to help all people, and especially young people, women, and vulnerable groups, to acquire the knowledge and skills they need for rewarding employment in a diversifying economy; recognize that the robust health and well-being of the population is essential to the country’s economic future; support Turkmen authorities to strengthen the health and social protection system performance and enhance spending to deliver higher quality and more inclusive services for all people. Strengthened governance of these sectors, including budgetary processes, will create conditions for sustainable, inter-sectoral action for health, education and social protection connecting national, regional (velayat) and local (etrap) levels.

sp.name: NUTRITION, FOOD SECURITY AND SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE
sp.description: By strengthening health interventions to address all forms of malnutrition, and by increasing the dietary diversity of women of reproductive age and children under five, the UNSDCF will seek to break the intergenerational cycle of malnutrition. This will be achieved through improved quality of nutrition, water and sanitation services, and hygiene practices, creating an enabling environment for faster development of cognitive capacities needed at early childhood stage and for improved health and education outcomes of the population, in particular of children, adolescents and pregnant women. Focusing on increasing and diversifying the production and productivity of smallholder farmers, fishers and agri-food producers, through climate-resilient and sustainable farming practices, the UNSDCF will support increasing food security and resilience to shocks, in particular for female farmers and rural youth, and reducing poverty, including through social protection programmes, while protecting land and ocean resources. The capacity of the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries and other relevant public and private institutions will be strengthened to explore ways to assure customary and formal tenure of smallholder male and female farmers

sp.name: SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES AND DECENT WORK FOR ALL
sp.description: Focusing on the policies, institutional framework, incentives and investments needed to transform the economy and develop sustainable pathways, the UNSDCF will contribute to diversifying the economy, creating decent jobs and including the marginalized active population, in particular youth and women, in a sustainable and just economy.

sp.name: EARLY CHILHOOD DEVELOPMENT AND LIFE-LONG LEARNING OUTCOMES AND SKILLS
sp.description:
By promoting early childhood education and supporting capacities to develop access to early childhood development, the UNSDCF will support Timor-Leste in laying the foundations for children’s learning and well-being. Furthermore, by increasing access to inclusive, equitable and quality basic and secondary education and its completion, creating innovative pathways for learning and developing foundational, transferable, digital and job-specific skills, the UNSDCF will seek to achieve greater learning outcomes for all, including those excluded from the traditional 
education system. Accelerated progress in this direction will result in a balanced set of capabilities for children to become economically productive, develop sustainable livelihoods, contribute to peaceful and democratic societies, enhance individual well-being, transform gender norms and relationships and reduce poverty and inequalities.

sp.name: QUALITY HEALTH CARE AND WELL-BEING
sp.description:
The UNSDCF will support greater and equitable access to PHC services with a view to helping Timor-Leste achieve universal health coverage, including in times of emergency, resulting in improved outcomes for health including sexual and reproductive health, continued reduction of maternal and neonatal mortality, eradication of tuberculosis and reduction of NCDs. Under this priority, the UNSDCF will also seek to increase health financing to support the development and retention of a trained health workforce, improve access to essential medicine and reduce the cost of health services and the financial hardship from out-of-pocket expenditures, including 
through social protection programmes and services.

sp.name: ACCOUNTABLE, INCLUSIVE AND PARTICIPATORY GOVERNANCE AND QUALITY PUBLIC SERVICES
sp.description: To ensure transparent, inclusive, accountable and gender-responsive governance systems that are focused on people’s rights and needs, the UNSDCF will support the consolidation of public institutions and increasing people’s democratic participation, particularly the excluded or under-represented, such as the rural poor, women, children and migrants. The intended result is not only access to the rule of law and public services for all people of Timor-Leste but also social cohesion and an end to violence against women and children.

sp.name: SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND RESILIENCE TO CLIMATE CHANGE
sp.description: The UNSDCF aims to ensure the sustainability of development progress in Timor-Leste by strengthening the ability of its institutions and communities to adapt to climate change and manage the risks of natural disasters, to mitigate their impacts on people’s lives, livelihoods, services and infrastructure, while preserving its natural resources.

sp.name: People
sp.description: This strategic priority sees the UN working to improve the well-being of Tanzanians, both now and in the future. This healthy, educated population will have improved capabilities and be far better equipped to support realisation of the country’s Middle-Income Country (MIC) aspirations.

sp.name: Prosperity
sp.description: The UN focus under the prosperity priority is on increasing production, productivity and incomes, helping to accelerate the creation of decent formal sector jobs at the individual level. Additionally, it seeks structural transformation and higher levels of economic growth at the national level, a key focus of the Five-Year Development Plan 2021/22-2025/26 (FYDP III) and Zanzibar.

sp.name: Planet
sp.description: The third strategic priority is towards supporting a greener, more sustainable development path. This includes better access to clean energy and technology to fuel growth, enabling more sustainable management of Tanzania’s wealth of natural resources. It will also cultivate close partnerships with government and communities to mitigate against climate change and reduce disaster risks.

sp.name: Enabling Environment
sp.description: This strategic priority supports the realisation of the results across the other areas. The priority focus is on broader issues of representative and inclusive governance, accessing data, development planning and financing, access to justice, access to information, sustaining peace, and the expansion and mainstreaming of gender equality and human rights.

oc.parentName: People
oc.name: By 2027, people in the United Republic of Tanzania, especially the most vulnerable, increasingly utilise quality gender transformative, inclusive and integrated basic education, health (with particular focus on RMNCAH, AIDS, TB, malaria, & epidemic prone diseases), nutrition, WASH and protection services.
oc.description: The people outcome contributes to the FYDP III pillar on Social Development and Infrastructure as well as the Human Capital and Social Development pillar of the 2021-2026 ZADEP. In the FYDP III, the interventions on human development focus on quality and relevant education, health, nutrition, social protection, water supply and sanitation. Under this outcome, the UN will contribute to the national development agenda by working to ensure that “by 2027, people in the United Republic of Tanzania, especially the most vulnerable, increasingly utilise quality gender transformative, inclusive and integrated basic education, health (with particular focus on RMNCAH, AIDS, TB, malaria, and epidemic prone diseases), nutrition, WASH and protection services.” The UN system in Tanzania will continue to address thematic areas with poorly performing demographic indicators as identified in the CCA.

oc.parentName: Prosperity
oc.name: By 2027 People in the United Republic of Tanzania working in MSMEs and small-scale agriculture, especially the most vulnerable, achieve increased, more sustainable productivity and incomes with more equitable access to productive resources.
oc.description: The prosperity outcome contributes to the national FYDP III economic growth and infrastructure pillars, as well as the economic transformation pillar of ZADEP. The outcome is specifically aligned to the interventions for deepening industrialisation and service provision, together with investment and trade promotion in the FYDP III, particularly those related to agriculture, manufacturing, science technology and innovation, and the blue economy. The CCA shows that economic growth is primarily benefitting wealthier urban households. As a result of the UN system’s commitment to ensuring that no one is left behind, a key focus of this outcome is on ensuring that the majority of Tanzanians who are engaged and depend on smallholder agriculture and in MSMEs for their livelihoods – also benefit through increased incomes and productivity. These two activities contribute significantly to Tanzania’s objective to achieve upper middle-income economy status

oc.parentName: Planet
oc.name: By 2027, people in the United Republic of Tanzania, especially the most vulnerable, contribute to and benefit from more inclusive and gender-responsive management of natural resources, climate change resilience, disaster risk reduction and increased use of efficient renewable energy.
oc.description: The third outcome of the UNSDCF contributes to the FYDP III interventions on inclusive development, environmental sustainability and climate change. It is aligned with the ZADEP pillars on governance and resilience, environment and climate change and safety, security and disaster management. The outcome seeks to ensure that “by 2027, people in the United Republic of Tanzania, especially the most vulnerable contribute to, and benefit from more inclusive and gender-responsive management of natural resources, climate change resilience, and increased use of efficient renewable energy”.

oc.parentName: Enabling Environment
oc.name: By 2027 people in the United Republic of Tanzania, especially the most vulnerable, participate in and benefit from government institutions and systems that promote peace and justice, are gender responsive, inclusive, accountable and representative, and are compliant with international human rights norms and standards.
oc.description: The enabling environment outcome is aligned to the interventions for human development in the FYDP III, where the focus is on good governance and rule of law, effective and efficient justice service delivery system, peace security and political stability. It contributes to the governance and resilience pillar of the ZADEP. Under this outcome the UN will work to support the renewal of the social contract and to support the closing of the gap between the people and the institutions that serve them as outlined in the Secretary General’s report on “Our Common Agenda.” Towards this, the UN will work on ensuring that “By 2027 the most vulnerable, participate in and benefit from government institutions and systems that promote peace and justice, are gender responsive, inclusive, accountable and representative, and are compliant with international human rights norms and standards”.

ou.name: Social Protection systems and services strengthened for expanded and improved coverage of the most vulnerable groups, incl. women, children, youth, older persons, persons with disability and regular migrants.
ou.description:
During the reporting period, in March 2022 the mainland Government reviewed and updated the national social protection policy and implementing strategy. The Government conducted five consultations with  different stakeholders from social assistance; social security; productive inclusion and social insurances.  Currently a cabinet paper has been drafted to be submitted to the cabinet. 
The mid-term review of the  productive social safety net program was successfully carried out in January 2022. PSSN II has expanded coverage from 70 percent to 100 percent to all villages and Shehia in mainland and Zanzibar with an estimated 5,180,684  beneficiaries of which 55.7 percent were females and 44.3 percent were males. The total number of households is 1,375,107.  PSSN II impact evaluation design was completed, and the survey questionnaire developed. A total of 434 villages from 32 PAAs were sampled for the evaluation. Training of enumerators on questionnaire management was done and completed and enumerators deployed to conduct data collection in sampled areas.  Total of 60,779 beneficiaries out of 97,430 were found with high level of disability and confirmed as being eligible for disability benefit and  45,875 disability beneficiaries were paid during the  July/August payment period in 2022.
