Strengthening Systems
sp.description:
Result 2.1: National capacities are strengthened and use data for efficient crisis response and recovery planning. Indicative intervention areas:
•	Data generation to inform recovery planning and implementation: In partnership with the government and relevant line ministries and authorities the UN will support sector assessments that will be used to inform national recovery planning and implementation. Examples include assessments related to human impact, war damage, gender, protection, monitoring environmental impact of war, energy systems, WASH systems, market and value chain, agri-business, forestry, nuclear installations, etc. 
•	Institutional capacity development for national partners: The government’s strong response to the impact of the war has demonstrated that past investments in institutions have resulted in strong systems. The UN will continue to support government institutions and ministries to further grow capacity and adapt and adjust to the new challenging context. Key sectors targeted for support and institutional capacity development include security, justice, agriculture, education, health, social protection, and environment sectors. The focus of capacity strengthening will be on leading crisis management, emergency response and recovery planning and implementation. Government capacity for protecting and monitoring human rights and documenting violations, and implementing commitments under the Women, Peace and Security Agenda and Youth, Peace and Security Agenda, will also be supported as will strengthening capacity of local civil society and volunteer groups to participate and engage in emergency response and early recovery. Provision of technical expertise for macro-economic forecasting and policy advocacy from an LNOB perspective will also be a focus area.

Result 2.2: Early recovery interventions are effective in increasing inclusive human development, promoting a sustainable green economy and building a resilient society. Indicative intervention areas:

•	Infrastructure Reconstruction: Mine action, debris removal, reconstruction of critical infrastructure (health centres, schools, WASH, agriculture, IT, etc), implementation of affordable housing solutions.
•	Social Protection: Support to strengthening national social protection systems, including child protection systems, and promotion of alignment of multipurpose cash assistance to existing national systems.  
•	Education: Safe, secure and inclusive learning, integrated approaches to psychosocial support, social and emotional learning, and life skills education, continuity of learning, reintegration of teachers, researchers and scientists.
•	Health: Recovery and transformation of health systems, including access to pharmaceuticals and vaccinations, cold chain systems strengthening, WASH systems, digital healthcare solutions to improve access to and the quality of maternal and child healthcare services, support to mental health services, and prosthetics for victims of war.  
•	Food Security:  Maintain critical food production systems and support agri-food supply chains, markets and exports. Expand capacity for agricultural product storage and export.
•	Livelihoods and Economic Growth: Income solutions for IDPs, war affected and most vulnerable, support to affected women and youth in livelihoods recovery, skills development, business support, entrepreneurship training, access to finance, networks, markets and culture. Mobilize the private sector in humanitarian response. Strengthen labour market governance focusing on decent work. Sustainable industrial recovery, development of competitive and resource-efficient processing industries.
•	Energy and Environment: Winterization, mitigating the energy crisis, preparedness for next heating season. Connecting buildings to energy monitoring tools and energy efficient technologies. Support to energy system repair and reconstruction. Environmental clean-up and remediation, clean transport and green reconstruction. Promote bio-energy use in agriculture, sustainable natural resource management. Sustainable and inclusive environmental governance and advocacy on environmental impact of war.

ou.name: Data generation
ou.description: •	Data Generation: In collaboration with the government and relevant ministries, the UN will assist in conducting sector assessments to inform inclusive national recovery planning and implementation. This will include the generation, analysis, and utilization of high-quality data, including gender and LNOB data. Notable assessments include RDNA 3, Voluntary National Review, the SIDAR housing damage database, the Social Cohesion and Reconciliation (SCORE) Index, the SCORE-inspired Holistic Assessment of Resilience of Population (SHARP), the Human Rights Progress Study, Country Gender Equality Profile, satellite imagery for monitoring cultural heritage damage, Condition of Return Assessment, General Population Survey, Mobility and Needs Assessment, Rapid Needs Assessment, Solid Fuel Assessment, Area Baseline for registered IDPs, Intentions and Perspectives of IDPs in Ukraine, and ad-hoc investigations related to community participation and shifting conditions, etc.

ou.name: Institutional capacity development
ou.description: •	Institutional Capacity Development: The government’s strong response to the impact of the war has demonstrated that past investments in institutions have resulted in strong systems. The UN will continue to support government institutions and ministries to further grow capacity and adapt to the new challenging context. Key sectors targeted for support and institutional capacity development include security, trade transport connectivity, justice, agriculture, science, innovations, culture, media, public administration, urban, digital transformation, human capital development, rule of law, anticorruption/integrity and responding to organised crime, the care economy, and others. Government capacity for protecting and monitoring human rights and documenting violations, reinforce social cohesion and inclusion, and implementing commitments under the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) Agenda, especially women’s meaningful role in decision making processes, and Youth, Peace and Security Agenda will also be supported.

ou.description: Capacity strengthening of regional and local authorities for good governance, inclusive and gender-responsive planning and budgeting, crisis management, emergency preparedness and response, outreach, advocacy and resource mobilization; strengthening capacity of local civil society, especially women’s rights/led organizations, self-help and volunteer groups, and organizations representing vulnerable groups to ensure their inclusion in the emergency response and community recovery efforts; and strengthening capacities of local media to promote social cohesion and provide fact-checked information to the population and as a form of protection against mis- and disinformation.

sp.name: Effective governance and justice for all
sp.description:
Effective governance and justice for all, achieving good governance with a focus on transparency and accountability principles that encompasses effective institutions, rule of law, anti-corruption, human rights, gender equality, labour rights, participatory and evidence-based decision-making, leaving no one behind and providing equitable access to public services and justice as pre-requisites for social and economic transformation within society.
For effective governance and justice systems that fulfill their obligations as duty bearers of human rights, the Cooperation Framework will strive to empower state institutions at all levels to effectively design, finance and implement gender-sensitive, human rights and evidence-based public legislation and policies which promote effective participation of the most vulnerable in an inclusive, transparent and accountable manner, and to ensure all people in Uzbekistan, especially the most vulnerable, benefit from increased and more equitable access to effective justice and human rights protection mechanisms.

sp.name: Inclusive human capital development leading to health, well-being and resilient prosperity
sp.description:
Inclusive human capital development leading to health, well-being and resilient prosperity focused on building a society where human capital development, the generation of employment and equal socio-economic opportunities for women and men, and the promotion of full access to quality social protection and health and education services, especially for most vulnerable and those at risk, are a reality, while reducing regional inequalities.
Cooperation in this area focuses on promoting improved livelihoods, decent work and expanding enabling opportunities generated by inclusive economic growth. It also includes enhancing access to inclusive, equitable and gender-sensitive quality health, education and social services for women, youth, children, persons with disabilities and other most vulnerable and at-risk groups of population. These elements are particularly key to a people-centred recovery from the COVID-19 socio-economic shock.

sp.name: Sustainable, climate-responsible and resilient development
sp.description:
Sustainable, climate-responsible and resilient development where actions are taken to promote effective and sustainable management of natural resources while supporting nature-based resilient development and effective and gender-responsive climate action at local level.
Considering the cascading effect of climate change and scarce natural resources on the livelihoods and well-being of the population and the subsequent impact on achieving Uzbekistan’s national economic and development priorities, including the national SDGs, the United Nations will cooperate with the Government and all relevant stakeholders towards the increased resilience of the most at-risk regions and communities to climate change and disasters. More sustainable and efficient use and management of natural resources and infrastructure, enhanced climate action, environmental governance and protection are expected to bring Uzbekistan a step closer to achieving sustainable, climate-responsible and resilient development and ensure a greener post-pandemic recovery.

sp.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY AREA  1: HUMAN DEVELOPMENT
sp.description: This area aims to contribute to Mozambique’s priority to develop human capital and social justice. It encompasses addressing gaps in gender equality, people’s equitable access to health, nutritious food, WASH, quality education and learning, and social protection, particularly for women and youth, people with disabilities, people and communities in the most vulnerable and marginalized situations, including by addressing harmful practices and gender norms.

sp.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY AREA  2: ECONOMIC DIVERSIFICATION AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS
sp.description: This area aims to contribute Mozambique’s priority to boost economic growth, productivity and job generation. It focuses on pursuing an accelerated shift towards more diversified, sustainable and inclusive economic growth, with increased and equitable opportunities for decent jobs and livelihoods and increased incomes, especially for women and youth, people with disabilities and displaced, the most vulnerable and marginalised.

sp.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY AREA  3: CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF NATURAL RESOURCES
sp.description: This area aims to contribute to Mozambique’s priority to strengthen sustainable management of natural resources and the environment. It focuses on accelerating actions on climate change mitigation and adaptation as well as disaster resilience. It prioritises improving the sustainable management of natural resources to enhance the resilience of infrastructure and human settlements and improve national productivity and GDP. It pays special attention to women and youth, people with disabilities, the most vulnerable and marginalised, and their rights to access information, participation and justice in environmental matters, as per Principle 10 of the Rio Declaration.

sp.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY AREA  4: PEACEBUILDING, HUMAN RIGHTS AND INCLUSIVE GOVERNANCE
sp.description: This area aims to contribute to Mozambique’s priorities to strengthen democracy and national unity, promote good governance and decentralisation, and enhance international cooperation with special attention to women and youth, IDPs, people with disabilities, the most vulnerable and marginalised. It encompasses promoting peace and greater social cohesion through more inclusive, participatory and accountable governance and institutions for people to enjoy their human rights and access an equitable and fair justice system.

ou.description:
UNDP:
UNDP has been working with the Malawi Electoral Commission to conduct a post-2020 electoral review process and consolidate the gains.  This includes the review of electoral laws and building capacities of MEC staff. UNDP has also supported the Center for Multiparty Democracy (CMD) to assist Political party dialogue and conflict prevention activities during by-elections conducted in 2021. Furthermore,  UNDP has engaged in a drive to digitalize the Parliament of Malawi to ensure that it is effective and efficient in delivering its representative, oversight, and legislative roles. 

UN Women: Supported capacity strengthening through training of district and community level stakeholder i.e., District Gender Technical working group and 10 Village Development Committees in Rumphi District. These are supporting implementation of UNSCR 1325 by ensuring women’s inclusion and participation in conflict prevention and peace building, women's participation in leadership in community structures such as VDCs and ADCs, including prevention of Gender Based Violence as a women's peace and security issue. These groups are expected to continue supporting gendered responses in security and humanitarian responses in the district. A total of 135 (108 Female and 27 Male) were trained and supported to engage at community level to support peace building and conflict prevention.

oc.name: By 2025, Malaysia has strengthened democratic governance, and all people living in Malaysia benefit from a more cohesive society, strengthened governance and participation.
oc.description:
There has been an overall shift in Malaysia’s development planning focus from “macroeconomic resilience” to “more meaningful economic growth”34. A key tenet of this shift is embedded in governance reform through greater transparency and public-service efficiency35. A focus on good governance, accountability and transparency, at the institutional and individual level, and keeping social consciousness and environmental sustainability at the centre of economic growth have been identified as being critical to Malaysia escaping the “middle-income trap” and achieving its full potential, in line with the priorities of SDG 16, including peace/social cohesion, governance and human rights. The MTR of the Eleventh Plan lays out a holistic and high-impact agenda for governance reforms, reflecting the broad need for greater separation of powers across the executive, legislature and judiciary, strengthening checks and balances, and other specific aspects, including electoral reforms, strengthening anticorruption efforts, etc. The SPV 2030 also reinforces these reforms as continuing priorities.

One of the hallmarks of a democratic nation can be seen in the degree of independence, transparency and inclusivity of its institutions, as noted in the MTR of the Eleventh Plan’s agenda for governance reforms, and the inclusivity of its political processes — processes which, in essence, determine and reflect the ultimate will and representation of the people. These processes are seen in electoral institutions that are inclusive and responsive to the population, political parties that reflect the spectrum of values and ideologies of the society, and legislative bodies that are truly representative. The “Sustaining Peace and Good Governance Goal” (SDG 16) has specific significance for parliamentarians. SDG 16 aims to “promote peaceful and inclusive societies, providing access to justice for all and building effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels”, with targets 16.6 and 16.7 directly fitting with parliamentarian roles. Another important element is space for civil society, dissenting voices and freedom of media, which has regained ground in recent times, to be further consolidated and professionalised. In this regard, the Ministry of Home Affairs is in the process of amending the Printing Presses and Publications Act 1984. Malaysia’s legal framework should provide increased protection against discrimination, abuse, stigmatisation and harassment on the basis of age, gender, race, disability or other characteristics, and this protection should be effectively enforced.

The focus on greater accountability in the governance pillar of the MTR of the Eleventh Plan also means expanding public participation in policymaking, ensuring that development plans are inclusive, and taking into account local contexts and constituency-specific realities. Therefore, any significant reform of governance policies must necessarily touch on challenging issues, emphasising the need for inclusive engagement with stakeholders. The role of civil society in governance reform is vital in terms of it playing a constructive role in policy debates on reform, thereby ensuring inclusion as well as making civil society a partner in monitoring governance performance and in delivering public services to specific target communities.

The current state of federal-state-local government relations is also key. There is a need for increased policy coherence and implementation coordination across levels of government in order to enhance the effectiveness of development results in Malaysia. Thus, a clearer understanding of the linkages between processes and stronger and more extensive engagement at subnational levels are entry points for intervention.

Also important is the fact that, although Malaysia’s various plans and policies have articulated variations on the themes of social stability, social integration and social cohesion, the overall scope remains quite limited. In line with the MTR of the Eleventh Plan, a National Unity Advisory Council has been formed and emphasis has been placed on a needs-based approach and, with the SPV 2030, on equitable outcomes. In March 2020, a new Ministry of National Unity was formed to take this important agenda forward. Consistent engagement at all levels (policy, institutional and community) is required to holistically address these issues and ensure inclusion.

The COVID-19 crisis has disproportionately impacted poor and vulnerable groups. Malaysia recorded a spike in gender-based violence (GBV), and the lack of routine data collection and inclusion of GBV in national surveys hampers efforts to mitigate its prevalence in an effective manner. The pandemic has further deepened the issues faced by undocumented persons, migrants, refugees and asylum seekers – in relation to legal access to services and squalid living conditions that have put them at greater risk of infection.

Finally, it is essential to note that the inclusion and participation of women, youth and children remains a major challenge. This is evidenced by the low political participation of women (as measured by their active engagement and parity in leadership positions or in the legislature). For instance, while women make up almost 60 per cent of the civil service (excluding the police and the military), the 14th General Elections of 2018 and the current Government brought about only five women ministers and four deputy ministers (12.9 per cent); 14.4 per cent of seats in the lower house of Parliament, and only 19.4 per cent of seats in the upper house36. In the corporate sector, women only hold 15.7 per cent of board seats in publicly-listed companies (against a target of 30 per cent)37. Youth under 3038 also constitute a significant proportion of Malaysia’s population, and, with the recent lowering of the voting age to 18, youth will form a significant proportion of the electorate in the future. Currently, there are inadequate opportunities for the engagement and participation of adolescents in national and subnational decision-making processes that affect their well-being, as well as in political processes. Responding to these challenges will be key to: ensuring that the potential of Malaysia’s youthful human capital is maximised; building a cohesive, inclusive and caring society; and developing values and gender and social norms to allow young people to feel that they have a stake in the nation’s development, and that they have the power and opportunity to contribute to decision-making that affects them. Hence, additional targeted interventions aimed at youth participation are needed, especially in decision making, productive work, social cohesion and political processes.

oc.parentName: Peace
oc.name: By 2025, Malaysia has strengthened democratic governance, and all people living in Malaysia benefit from a more cohesive society, strengthened governance and participation.
oc.description:
There has been an overall shift in Malaysia’s development planning focus from “macroeconomic resilience” to “more meaningful economic growth”34. A key tenet of this shift is embedded in governance reform through greater transparency and public-service efficiency35. A focus on good governance, accountability and transparency, at the institutional and individual level, and keeping social consciousness and environmental sustainability at the centre of economic growth have been identified as being critical to Malaysia escaping the “middle-income trap” and achieving its full potential, in line with the priorities of SDG 16, including peace/social cohesion, governance and human rights. The MTR of the Eleventh Plan lays out a holistic and high-impact agenda for governance reforms, reflecting the broad need for greater separation of powers across the executive, legislature and judiciary, strengthening checks and balances, and other specific aspects, including electoral reforms, strengthening anticorruption efforts, etc. The SPV 2030 also reinforces these reforms as continuing priorities.

One of the hallmarks of a democratic nation can be seen in the degree of independence, transparency and inclusivity of its institutions, as noted in the MTR of the Eleventh Plan’s agenda for governance reforms, and the inclusivity of its political processes — processes which, in essence, determine and reflect the ultimate will and representation of the people. These processes are seen in electoral institutions that are inclusive and responsive to the population, political parties that reflect the spectrum of values and ideologies of the society, and legislative bodies that are truly representative. The “Sustaining Peace and Good Governance Goal” (SDG 16) has specific significance for parliamentarians. SDG 16 aims to “promote peaceful and inclusive societies, providing access to justice for all and building effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels”, with targets 16.6 and 16.7 directly fitting with parliamentarian roles. Another important element is space for civil society, dissenting voices and freedom of media, which has regained ground in recent times, to be further consolidated and professionalised. In this regard, the Ministry of Home Affairs is in the process of amending the Printing Presses and Publications Act 1984. Malaysia’s legal framework should provide increased protection against discrimination, abuse, stigmatisation and harassment on the basis of age, gender, race, disability or other characteristics, and this protection should be effectively enforced.

The focus on greater accountability in the governance pillar of the MTR of the Eleventh Plan also means expanding public participation in policymaking, ensuring that development plans are inclusive, and taking into account local contexts and constituency-specific realities. Therefore, any significant reform of governance policies must necessarily touch on challenging issues, emphasising the need for inclusive engagement with stakeholders. The role of civil society in governance reform is vital in terms of it playing a constructive role in policy debates on reform, thereby ensuring inclusion as well as making civil society a partner in monitoring governance performance and in delivering public services to specific target communities.

The current state of federal-state-local government relations is also key. There is a need for increased policy coherence and implementation coordination across levels of government in order to enhance the effectiveness of development results in Malaysia. Thus, a clearer understanding of the linkages between processes and stronger and more extensive engagement at subnational levels are entry points for intervention.

Also important is the fact that, although Malaysia’s various plans and policies have articulated variations on the themes of social stability, social integration and social cohesion, the overall scope remains quite limited. In line with the MTR of the Eleventh Plan, a National Unity Advisory Council has been formed and emphasis has been placed on a needs-based approach and, with the SPV 2030, on equitable outcomes. In March 2020, a new Ministry of National Unity was formed to take this important agenda forward. Consistent engagement at all levels (policy, institutional and community) is required to holistically address these issues and ensure inclusion.

The COVID-19 crisis has disproportionately impacted poor and vulnerable groups. Malaysia recorded a spike in gender-based violence (GBV), and the lack of routine data collection and inclusion of GBV in national surveys hampers efforts to mitigate its prevalence in an effective manner. The pandemic has further deepened the issues faced by undocumented persons, migrants, refugees and asylum seekers – in relation to legal access to services and squalid living conditions that have put them at greater risk of infection.

Finally, it is essential to note that the inclusion and participation of women, youth and children remains a major challenge. This is evidenced by the low political participation of women (as measured by their active engagement and parity in leadership positions or in the legislature). For instance, while women make up almost 60 per cent of the civil service (excluding the police and the military), the 14th General Elections of 2018 and the current Government brought about only five women ministers and four deputy ministers (12.9 per cent); 14.4 per cent of seats in the lower house of Parliament, and only 19.4 per cent of seats in the upper house36. In the corporate sector, women only hold 15.7 per cent of board seats in publicly-listed companies (against a target of 30 per cent)37. Youth under 3038 also constitute a significant proportion of Malaysia’s population, and, with the recent lowering of the voting age to 18, youth will form a significant proportion of the electorate in the future. Currently, there are inadequate opportunities for the engagement and participation of adolescents in national and subnational decision-making processes that affect their well-being, as well as in political processes. Responding to these challenges will be key to: ensuring that the potential of Malaysia’s youthful human capital is maximised; building a cohesive, inclusive and caring society; and developing values and gender and social norms to allow young people to feel that they have a stake in the nation’s development, and that they have the power and opportunity to contribute to decision-making that affects them. Hence, additional targeted interventions aimed at youth participation are needed, especially in decision making, productive work, social cohesion and political processes.

sp.name: Strategic Priority 1 - GOVERNANCE, HUMAN RIGHT, PEACE & SECURITY
sp.description:
Strategic Intent: All Nigerians enjoy good and inclusive governance and human rights in secure, resilient and peaceful communities.
The  UN system in Nigeria will place premium and special focus on increasing citizens confidence and engagement in governance and public service delivery mechanisms, by supporting the fight against corruption and reinforcing the accountability framework.

The UN system will leverage on its networks and partnerships with stakeholders to provide quality advisory service, youth and women participation in peace processes, capacity strengthening, and technical support for conflict prevention, mediation and reconciliation, psychosocial support through the establishment of early warning mechanisms/responses and the national peace architecture.

sp.name: Strategic Priority 2 - Equitable Quality Basic Services
sp.description:
Strategic Intent: Nigerians enjoy improved well-being through sustainable, equitable and quality basic social and protection services which fulfill their human rights and contribute to greater social cohesion and economic development.

The UN system in Nigeria envisions that all Nigerians will realize their human rights and access quality basic services in an equitable manner. Availability and accessibility of sustainable, equitable and quality basic social protection services will contribute to greater social cohesion and economic development. Since the result area covers several sectors, the specific strategies chosen in a particular year will depend on the needs, geographic focus and a balance between upstream policy work and downstream implementation.

sp.name: Strategic Priority 3 - Sustainable Inclusive Economic Growth & Development
sp.description:
Strategic intent: Nigerians have improved living standard characterized by inclusive and diversified economic growth, effective population management, food security and environmental sustainability.

The UN System will assist Nigeria to address the identified challenges in this result area, through joint action and based on its comparative advantage by mobilizing support to develop appropriate policies, plans and regulatory frameworks aimed at sustainable and inclusive economic growth and development in the country. The UN will support the Government in this result area by providing strategic interventions for the diversification of the economy, effective management and utilization of human resources, food security and environmental sustainability.

oc.name: Outcome 1.1 - Good Governance and Rule of Law
oc.description: Good governance and the rule of law are essential preconditions for the fulfillment of peace and stability, without which societies cannot function, let alone flourish. The commitment to transparency and accountability mitigates corruption and reinforces rule of law. Hence creating economic opportunities which in turn stimulates growth.

oc.parentName: Strategic Priority 1 - GOVERNANCE, HUMAN RIGHT, PEACE & SECURITY
oc.name: Outcome 1.2 - Humanitarian Response, Peacebuilding and Security
oc.description: Humanitarian response, peace-building and security are interlinked because humanitarian action can be seen as a building block for peace by providing basic services, reducing tensions, creating a space for dialogue, and putting people’s basic needs at the center of operations. Both humanitarian and peace-building actors would benefit from exploring further how humanitarian action can contribute to creating the conditions necessary for sustaining peace.

oc.name: Outcome 2.1 - Health, Nutrition, and HIV/AIDS
oc.description: While health, including nutrition and access to HIV services, is a basic human right, the majority of Nigerians have limited access to realize this entitlement. Through the UNSDCF UN will contribute towards addressing the challenges in health, nutrition, and HIV/AIDS sectors. So it is expected that by 2022, Nigerians , with focus on most disadvantaged, have access and use quality health, nutrition and HIV & AIDS services.

oc.parentName: Sustained and inclusive economic and social development
oc.name: Outcome 1: Inclusive Prosperity
oc.description:
Outcome 1: The UN entities contribution to inclusive prosperity of North Macedonia focus on creating new productive, full-time jobs that are resilient to any sustained or future shocks, supporting the authorities to make growth more robust, sustainable and inclusive. Interventions will prioritize LNOB groups of people who will be equipped with skills and capacities to enjoy and have equal access to full, productive and freely chosen employment, thus reducing inequalities, including income inequality. 

The UN entities contribution to inclusive prosperity of North Macedonia focus on creating new productive, full-time jobs that are resilient to any sustained or future shocks, supporting the authorities to make growth more robust, sustainable and inclusive. Interventions will prioritize LNOB groups of people who will be equipped with skills and capacities to enjoy and have equal access to full, productive and freely chosen employment, thus reducing inequalities, including income inequality.

oc.parentName: Sustained and inclusive economic and social development
oc.name: Outcome 2: Quality Services for All
oc.description:
Outcome 2: By 2025, people in North Macedonia have universal access to rights-based quality social services – healthcare, education, and necessary social and child protection - rooted in systems resilient to emergencies.

UN entities have committed to support the country’s social development through activities that will strive to achieve universal access to rights-based quality social services – healthcare, education, and  social and child protection, including in emergencies. While the activities will be targeting all people in the country, the nature of this outcome entails focus on the most vulnerable ones, those that are usually left behind.

oc.parentName: Climate action, natural resources and disaster risk management
oc.name: Outcome 3: Healthy Environment
oc.description:
Outcome 3: By 2025, people in North Macedonia benefit from ambitious climate action, sustainably managed natural resources and well-preserved biodiversity through good environmental governance and disaster resilient communities.

Over the period 2021-2025, the UN entities contribution to healthy environment will focus on policy support, capacity building and community actions for low-emission development and multi-sector resilience to climate change; sustainable and inclusive management of natural resources; prevention and response to air pollution threats, effective disaster risk reduction and response; waste reduction and efficient waste management, and reducing impact of the unsustainable farming practices on the lake/river watersheds.

oc.parentName: Transparent and accountable democratic governance
oc.name: Outcome 4: Good Governance
oc.description:
Outcome 4: By 2025, people in North Macedonia benefit from improved rule of law; evidence-based, anticipatory and gender-responsive policies; greater social cohesion; and effective service delivery by transparent, accountable and responsive institutions.

The UN in North Macedonia works with the government and whole of society towards effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels, and promotion and protection of human rights for all, focusing on groups that have been left behind, or are at risk of being left behind, including women, children, youth not in education, employment or training (NEET), persons with disabilities, Roma and other ethnic communities, refugees, asylum seekers, migrants, internally displaced persons (IDPs) and stateless, LGBTI persons, people in rural areas and small farmers, older persons and other vulnerable groups.

ou.parentName: Outcome 1: Inclusive Prosperity
ou.name: Output 1.1: Sustainable enterprises created as generators of employment
ou.description: Output 1.1: Sustainable enterprises created as generators of employment, through strengthened value chains and increased capacities to adopt new business models. Throughout 2021, under this output, UN will work with the stakeholders on creation of productive and competitive enterprises as generators of employment, decent work and innovations, by delivering tailored interventions for start-ups, formalization of economy and strengthening value chains. Focusing on youth at policy and at operational level, UN will also work with Government to enhance SMEs development and innovation ecosystem, including by introducing know-how and building capacity for technical modernization, while supporting public-private partnership to address the challenges of the adjusting employment patterns.

ou.parentName: Outcome 1: Inclusive Prosperity
ou.name: Output 1.2 Jobs for women and vulnerable people
ou.description: Outcome 1.2: Women and vulnerable/excluded persons benefit from supportive environment through tailored employment measures and a more dynamic and inclusive skilling system that responds to labour market needs for all people. Under this output, in 2021, UN will assist the Government to develop supportive environment for women and vulnerable/excluded persons through tailored activation and employment support measures and a more dynamic and inclusive skilling system that responds to labour market needs of all people. In that context, UN will pursue advocacy interventions to eliminate legal and administrative barriers to the access and inclusion of asylum seekers in job market, including evaluation of skills & diplomas.  Furthermore, UN will develop, support and promote life-long learning models among socially excluded groups, including people with disabilities, prisons inmates and Roma people with special focus on women.

ou.parentName: Outcome 1: Inclusive Prosperity
ou.name: Output 1.3 Enhanced policies and regulatory environment
ou.description: Output 1.3: Enhanced and gender-responsive policy and regulatory measures that foster entrepreneurship and financing for inclusive and green growth. in 2021, under this output, UN entities will work to enhance and harmonize policy and regulatory measures with the International labour standards and EU acquis, in order to foster gender-responsive, entrepreneurial and green growth. To achieve this, UN will support social dialogue as an essential element of the European social model, assisting the government and social partners to bridge the legal and implementation gaps in compliance with International Labour Standards and the EU acquis. The UN will facilitate tripartite consultations and give technical support for drafting the new National Employment Strategy and the new Action Plan on Youth Employment. Furthermore, UN will promote alternative social services and policy reforms for vulnerable, and enhance ESA’s capacity to provide services with strengthened consultation and environment that promotes future jobs and skills requested by the market. UN will work on developing and maintaining of MIS for more competitive, inclusive, efficient and resilient agri-food systems, as well as on optimizing the opportunities from Diaspora engagement.

ou.parentName: Outcome 1: Inclusive Prosperity
ou.name: Output 1.4 Under-employment, informality and protection at work
ou.description: Output 1.4: Improved quality of employment through measures for transition to formality and adequate protection at work in compliance with international labour standards. Limited activities under this output will be carried out during 2021, focusing on improving the quality of employment with pilot measures to reduce informality, technical support for drafting the new labour legislation,  and promotion of the ratification of the new international labour standards.

ou.parentName: Outcome 1: Inclusive Prosperity
ou.name: Output 1.5 Sustainable and competitive rural economy
ou.description: Output 1.5: Policies and capacities strengthened for sustainable and competitive rural economy aligned with EU, with focus on small farms and women farmers. Under this output, during 2021, UN will continue its work on strengthening evidence-based policies and institutional capacities for sustainable and competitive rural economy aligned with EU, focusing on land consolidation and implementation of other land market instruments, supporting small farm-holders and women farmers with integrated local development initiatives piloted in selected municipalities, sustainable production technologies, income diversification, and improving smallholders’ access to markets,  value chains and enhanced rural services.

ou.parentName: Outcome 2: Quality Services for All
ou.name: Output 2.1 Universal access to affordable high quality health services
ou.description: Output 2.1: Health system is strengthened to provide universal access to affordable high quality and people-centred services to promote healthy lifestyles and address population-specific health needs and risk factors, including in emergencies. The work of all involved UN entities in 2021 will aim to continue supporting the health care system for efficient delivery of affordable high quality and people-centered essential health services, including support in responding to the COVID-19 pandemic, in line with the Covid-19 Response Framework, developed in 2020.   UN will work on improvement of the health care coverage, through pilot interventions in primary health care. It will focus on all levels of productive health services, such as family planning, maternal health and cervical cancer prevention. These efforts will be coupled with improving prevention of specific conditions, awareness raising and improved access to services for women and girls and other vulnerable categories such are refugees, migrants and stateless people. In addition, functional analysis of home visiting system and pediatric care will be undertaken, Vaccine hesitancy at national level will be tackled, etc.  Extensive activities for capacity building of health workforce will be carried out in parallel. UN entities will further work on strengthening of the perinatal health care system through Implementation of various actions from the National Master Plan for perinatal care and provide policy support by strengthening the evidence-based policy making processes on health inequity, institutionalization of the National Health Accounts, Health financing and financial risk protection; development of parenting strategy; reversing childhood obesity trend and others. Finally, in the area of health, UN entities will support accelerated digitalization of the health system by introducing digital mental health tools; digitalization of the reporting and recording system for home visiting nurses and the vaccination registry system.

ou.parentName: Outcome 2: Quality Services for All
ou.name: Output 2.2 Quality and affordable education
ou.description: Output 2.2: Quality and affordable education is provided in trauma-informed, gender-responsive and inclusive learning environments to children and young people in the country to raise learning outcomes, enable their socio-emotional development and empower them with skills for transition to the labour market. in 2021, under this output, UN entities will provide support to the education reforms aimed at providing quality and affordable education in trauma-informed, gender-responsive and inclusive learning environments to children and young people in the country to raise learning outcomes, enable their socio-emotional development and empower them with skills for transition to the labour market. UN entities will focus on teachers capacity development, creation of digital and inclusive learning tools and resources that are in line with the pre-primary, primary and secondary education curricula, Improvements of WASH capacities in schools, awareness raising to remove barriers to inclusion of children with disabilities, as well as on piloting of the comprehensive sexuality education in selected schools. The entities will also undertake preparatory activities for introduction of youth initiative in municipalities that measures youth engagement and develop advocacy, knowledge exchange and community engagement on issues of interest and benefit of youth. Refugees, asylum seekers and stateless children will be supported to access the appropriate level of education.

ou.parentName: Outcome 2: Quality Services for All
ou.name: Output 2.3 Social protection of all persons in need
ou.description: Output 2.3: Social protection system is resilient to external shocks and strengthened to deliver progressively improved services to all persons in need, especially to those left behind. in 2021, under this output, Activities aimed to enhance the social protection system to increase its resilience to external shocks and to progressively strengthen the delivery of improved services to all persons in need, especially to those left behind will also be part of the UN agenda for 2021. The activities will include: enhanced provision of social protection services to vulnerable categories of migrants, asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons; new parenting programmes and helpline services including parenting services campaigns; support of the child-care system through capacity development of foster and kindship care, and creating community-based support system; development of community-based care/services for children and families experiencing adversity; Continuous child protection and GBV services and psychosocial support to children and families in emergencies as well as establishment of regional centers for ICF-based assessment for additional educational, health and social support to children and youth. Evaluation on UNICEF interventions for inclusion of children with disabilities will be undertaken, as well as analysis of multi-dimensional poverty aimed to provide better evidence for policy improvements, including enhancement of the national statistical system. Support to the introduction of social work case management mentoring and supervision will be provided, as well as technical assistance in the development of integrated MIS on social cash transfers and social services.

ou.parentName: Outcome 2: Quality Services for All
ou.name: Output 2.4 Eliminate all forms of violence
ou.description: Output 2.4: Improved multi-sectoral response to prevent and address all forms of violence based on victims/survivor-centred approach, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes. in 2021, under this output, UN entities will provide dedicated support for improved multisectoral response to prevent and address all forms of violence, using victims/survivor-centered approach and through operationalization of the Law on Prevention and Protection of Violence Against Women and Domestic Violence. UN entities will support the relevant partners in collection of disaggregated data and evidence for defining requirements and specifications of a system for GBV data integration. Service providers will be capacitated to provide better multi-sectorial response to GBV by implementing the standards enshrined in CEDAW and the Istanbul Convention, while the Civil Society Organizations will be capacitated to support the development and implementation of laws and policies in line with CEDAW and the Istanbul Convention and to promote favorable social norms, attitudes and behaviors to prevent violence against women and girls. UN entities will also work with community figures/leaders mobilized to enhance gender equality and women empowerment and design and implement cross-sectoral communication for development initiatives to address barriers to optimal thriving and flourishing of children.

ou.parentName: Outcome 3: Healthy Environment
ou.name: Output 3.1 Low-emissions development and climate change resilience
ou.description: Output 3.1: The enabling policy, regulatory environment, capacities at central and local level and community actions strengthened for low-emission development and multi-sector resilience to climate change. In 2021, the UN intends to support to country on policy development and implementation (support for development of new strategic policy documents  such as the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and greater implementation/enforcement of environment and climate change legislation, EU Chapter 27 requirements) and National Adaptation Plan, and implementation of priority measures), climate finance and green economy (support to Green Climate Fund (GCF) national mechanism and programme, potential implementation of the Green Financing Facility, a new vehicle to provide financing to end consumers for renewable energy and energy efficiency investments, assessment of potential for expansion of the use of clean technologies and creation of green jobs, acceleration of market transformation for industrial energy efficiency), and climate-smart agriculture (new technologies piloted, tools for evidence-based policy) and on public awareness and knowledge increasing. In addition, UN will support the introduction of environment/green education within the ongoing primary education reform, including by development of appropriate content, building capacities of more than 150 teachers, more than 50 education inspectors and raising awareness on env. and climate change of of the general public (>100,000 people).

ou.parentName: Outcome 3: Healthy Environment
ou.name: Output 3.2 Integrated, sustainable and inclusive management of natural resources
ou.description: Output 3.2: Solutions are identified and scaled-up at central and local levels for integrated, sustainable and inclusive management of natural resources (water, land, forests, biodiversity). in 2021, under this output, UN will provide support with a diverse set of activities related to land, forest and biodiversity protection (2 new protected areas mgt plans, increased forest area, policy for sustainable land tenure and management, 3’000 ha with sustainable land management practices, various activities for protection of forest vegetation, reptiles and amphibians, and sustainable use of non-timber forest products), enhanced food safety and quality standards in dairy sector, activities for greener Skopje (biotope mapping, green cadastre update, construction of green roofs, development of water strategy etc.), increased proportion of transboundary basin with operational arrangement for water cooperation, and cultural and natural heritage protection (increased total expenditure per capita (public and private), various activities to protect Cultural and Natural Heritage of the Ohrid Region. Last but not least, activities that ensure lake/river watersheds protection through promoting sustainable farming practices (Prespa: + 200 ha, +150 households, Strumica River Basin), sustainable tourism offer (+40 B&Bs in Prespa) and active transboundary governance of Prespa Lake Watershed (active Management Body and Water Management Working Group) will be continued.

ou.parentName: Outcome 3: Healthy Environment
ou.name: Output 3.3 Air pollution in urban areas decreased
ou.description:
Output 3.3: Capacities at central and local levels are strengthened to prevent and respond to the air pollution threats and health consequences in most vulnerable communities. 

In 2021 the UN’s support will focus on providing evidence for policy (preparation of Source Apportionment Study, Analyzing interlinkages between human mobility and air pollution study), raising public awareness (public awareness on air pollution causes and effects), improvement of the monitoring system for air pollution in Skopje, and demonstration/proof of concept for measures to reduce the air pollution in the City of Skopje (implementation of  energy efficiency measures in households in Lisiche settlement), support to regulatory changes to support policies for reduction of air pollution.

ou.parentName: Outcome 3: Healthy Environment
ou.name: Output 3.4 Effective disaster risk reduction and response
ou.description: Output 3.4: Capacities at central and local levels are strengthened to identify multi-hazard risks and to plan, finance and implement effective disaster risk reduction and response, including human displacement, in line with the Sendai framework. A comprehensive portfolio of DRR activities is planned for 2021, with focus on field activities (specific activities on increased resilience of Agri sector, improved flood risk management of the Drini River Basin (transboundary) and in the Polog region), capacity building of civil servants (capacity building on DRR (10 civil servants, urban focus) and on human displacement caused by disasters (200 civil servants, central level focus)), DRR finance (Flood Risk Financing and Flood Risk Transfer, Increase of public expenditures in DRR), early warning system (early warning system established in Polog region, 2 data informed and gender responsive DRR plans).

ou.parentName: Outcome 3: Healthy Environment
ou.name: Output 3.5 Waste reduction and efficient waste management
ou.description: Output 3.5: National and local capacities strengthened, and awareness increased for waste reduction and efficient waste management (chemical, water, municipal waste, hazardous waste, medical waste – including in rural areas). In 2021, the UN will continue to providing sizable support in the cleanup of environmental hotspots (Ohis Factory Complex: HCH waste, small waste basin).

ou.parentName: Outcome 4: Good Governance
ou.name: Output 4.1 Rule of Law, Access to Justice and Human rights
ou.description: Output 4.1: The rule of law, access to justice, and protection and promotion of human rights for all, especially those left behind advanced through inclusive and gender-responsive legal, policy, and institutional frameworks and strengthened capacities. Throughout 2021, the UN will strengthen its partnership and capacity of state and non-state actors to accelerate policy and institutional reforms advancing the rule of law, gender equality, and access to justice and services responsive to those in need. The empowerment of people left behind to claim and seek the protection of their rights and effective free legal aid will be central to these efforts.

ou.parentName: Outcome 4: Good Governance
ou.name: Output 4.2 Institutions capacitated for better planning, budgeting and service design and delivery
ou.description:
Output 4.2: Capacities of central and local governments strengthened to:
a)	better plan, budget, monitor and track expenditure and leverage resources in a gender-responsive manner in support of accelerated sustainable development 
b)	improve design and efficient delivery of quality public services (targeting excluded groups, including refugee /migration management)
with improved social accountability and participation in decision-making.  

UN will contribute in developing and implementing national strategies and legislation in line with international and EU standards in areas of non-discrimination, gender equality, migration management, judicial reform, anti-corruption, arms control and fight against organized crime. The government technical skills to engage in the EU accession negotiations will be stepped up, along with the support to the EU acquis approximation process.
  
At central and local government level, the UN will accelerate efficient delivery of quality public services targeting excluded groups and their social and economic vulnerabilities, thus improving the overall trust and accountability of institutions. Promoting transparency and participation in the decision-making will result in better planning, budgeting and monitoring, while leveraging resources in a gender-responsive and child-sensitive manner. The UN will support primary school optimization and improving the budgetary allocations system in primary and secondary education, as well as youth consultations and adolescent participation and empowerment.

ou.parentName: Outcome 4: Good Governance
ou.name: Output 4.3 Improved participatory policy making based on better data
ou.description: Output 4.3: Increased utilization of foresight and quality and disaggregated data for improved forward looking, evidence-based, results-oriented and transparent policy-making, responsive to the rights of women, men, girls and boys and vulnerabilities of the groups left behind, at all levels and in all contexts, including humanitarian. In 2021, UN will support national stakeholders to promote evidence-based policy making and long‐term strategic visioning that will accelerate SDGs mainstreaming and shaping of a National Development Strategy. To this end, foresight methods for strategic multi-year planning, responsive to the rights of women, men, girls and boys, and vulnerabilities of the groups left behind or at risk of being left behind in all contexts, including humanitarian, will be promoted. Data collection and analysis mechanisms will be strengthened as a key precondition for evidenced-based and result-oriented policy making.

ou.parentName: Outcome 4: Good Governance
ou.name: Output 4.4 Improved social cohesion and trust building
ou.description: Output 4.4: Social cohesion and trust improved through dialogue and meaningful participation by youth, women, ethnic and religious minorities, refugees, and other vulnerable groups. UN interventions are designed to support societal transformation for more active and responsible individual and community approaches to sustainable and inclusive development. The UN support to good governance, human rights and gender equality will ultimately contribute to strengthening the social cohesion and trust, through improved dialogue and meaningful participation.
